OSAPIOpenFile.documentation: An OS API function that opens a file for reading, writing, or both, and return a handle or descriptor that can be used to interact with the file.

OSAPIReadFile.label: OS API Read File
OSAPIReadFile.documentation: An OS API function that reads data from a file or input stream into memory.

OSAPIReadMemory.label: OS API Read Memory
OSAPIReadMemory.documentation: An OS API function that reads the contents of memory from a specific address or region.

OSAPIResumeProcess.label: OS API Resume Process
OSAPIResumeProcess.documentation: An OS API function that resumes the execution of a paused, stopped, or suspended process.

OSAPIResumeThread.label: OS API Resume Thread
OSAPIResumeThread.documentation: An OS API function that resumes the execution of a paused, stopped, or suspended thread.

OSAPISaveRegisters.label: OS API Save Registers
OSAPISaveRegisters.documentation: An OS API function that retrieves and saves the values of CPU registers for a specific process or thread.

OSAPISetRegisters.label: OS API Set Registers
OSAPISetRegisters.documentation: An OS API function that modifies the values of CPU registers.

OSAPISetThreadContext.label: OS API Set Thread Context
OSAPISetThreadContext.documentation: An OS API function that modifies the execution context of a thread.

OSAPISuspendProcess.label: OS API Suspend Process
OSAPISuspendProcess.documentation: An OS API function that pauses the execution of a process.

OSAPISuspendThread.label: OS API Suspend Thread
OSAPISuspendThread.documentation: An OS API function that pauses the execution of a thread.

OSAPISystemFunction.label: OS API System Function
OSAPISystemFunction.documentation: Indirect System calls are made through an OS-specific library (like glibc in Linux) that provides a higher-level API for the system calls.

OSAPITraceProcess.label: OS API Trace Process
OSAPITraceProcess.documentation: An OS API function that enables a program to monitor, control, or interact with the execution of a process.

OSAPITraceThread.label: OS API Trace Thread
OSAPITraceThread.documentation: An OS API function that enables a program to monitor, control, or interact with the execution of a thread.

OSAPIUnloadModule.label: OS API Unload Module
OSAPIUnloadModule.documentation: An OS API function that removes a previously loaded module from memory.

OSAPIWriteFile.label: OS API Write File
OSAPIWriteFile.documentation: An OS API function that writes data from a buffer in memory to a file or output stream.

OSAPIWriteMemory.label: OS API Write Memory
OSAPIWriteMemory.documentation: An OS API function that writes data into the memory space of another process or into specific regions of memory.

OTAbortCommand.label: OT Abort Command
OTAbortCommand.documentation: Commands a device to abort a service/program.

OTActuator.label: OT Actuator
OTActuator.documentation: An OT actuator is an industrial-grade actuator optimized for operational technology (OT) environments, such as SCADA or process-control systems. It tolerates harsher conditions, meets stricter safety and reliability standards, and integrates seamlessly with ICS protocols to enable real-time mechanical motion or adjustments in production lines and critical infrastructure.

OTAlarmMessage.label: OT Alarm Message
OTAlarmMessage.documentation: Report danger, hazards, or serious errors.

OTAlarmMessageEvent.label: OT Alarm Message Event
OTAlarmMessageEvent.documentation: Report danger, hazards, or serious errors.

OTChangeControlProgramCommand.label: OT Change Control Program Command
OTChangeControlProgramCommand.documentation: Commands a remote device to modify an existing control program.

OTChangeControlProgramCommandEvent.label: OT Change Control Program Command Event
OTChangeControlProgramCommandEvent.documentation: Commands a remote device to modify an existing control program.

OTChangeDataCommand.label: OT Change Data Command
OTChangeDataCommand.documentation: OT command that modifies existing data on a remote device.

OTChangeDataCommandEvent.label: OT Change Data Command Event
OTChangeDataCommandEvent.documentation: OT command that modifies existing data on a remote device.

OTConnectionCommand.label: OT Connection Command
OTConnectionCommand.documentation: Establish a network connection with a device.

OTConnectionCommandEvent.label: OT Connection Command Event
OTConnectionCommandEvent.documentation: Establish a network connection with a device.

OTControlCommand.label: OT Control Command
OTControlCommand.documentation: Command and control the managed process.

OTControlCommandEvent.label: OT Control Command Event
OTControlCommandEvent.documentation: Command and control the managed process.

OTControlFunction.label: OT Control Function
OTControlFunction.documentation: A function which accesses OT Control Variables

OTControlLogicProcess.label: OT Control Logic Process
OTControlLogicProcess.documentation: The instructions and algorithms within an OT Controller defined by user programming to interpret inputs, process information, and determine outputs.

OTControlProgram.label: OT Control Program
OTControlProgram.documentation: The file stored in controller memory that is used to operate the controller.

OTControlVariable.label: OT Control Variable
OTControlVariable.documentation: A control variable is the measurement of the physical condition of the device that influences the Process Variables.

OTController.label: OT Controller
OTController.documentation: An OT Controller is an industrial control device that automatically regulates one or more controlled variables in response to command inputs and real-time feedback signals.

OTControllerOperatingMode.label: OT Controller Operating Mode
OTControllerOperatingMode.documentation: The OT controller operating mode designates the specific, selectable state of an OT controller that delineates its operational behavior and governs access to engineering functions, commonly including Program, Run, Remote, Test, or Stop.

OTCreateDataCommand.label: OT Create Data Command
OTCreateDataCommand.documentation: OT command that creates data on a remote device.

OTCreateDataCommandEvent.label: OT Create Data Command Event
OTCreateDataCommandEvent.documentation: OT command that creates data on a remote device.

OTCreateNewControlProgramCommand.label: OT Create New Control Program Command
OTCreateNewControlProgramCommand.documentation: Commands a remote device to create an control program.

OTCreateNewControlProgramCommandEvent.label: OT Create New Control Program Command Event
OTCreateNewControlProgramCommandEvent.documentation: Commands a remote device to create an control program.

OTDebugCommand.label: OT Debug Command
OTDebugCommand.documentation: Investigate or analyze the current state of the system.

OTDebugCommandEvent.label: OT Debug Command Event
OTDebugCommandEvent.documentation: Investigate or analyze the current state of the system.

OTDeleteControlProgramCommand.label: OT Delete Control Program Command
OTDeleteControlProgramCommand.documentation: Commands a remote device to remove an existing control program.

OTDeleteControlProgramCommandEvent.label: OT Delete Control Program Command Event
OTDeleteControlProgramCommandEvent.documentation: Commands a remote device to remove an existing control program.

OTDeleteDataCommand.label: OT Delete Data Command
OTDeleteDataCommand.documentation: OT command that removes data on a remote device.

OTDeleteDataCommandEvent.label: OT Delete Data Command Event
OTDeleteDataCommandEvent.documentation: OT command that removes data on a remote device.

OTDeviceDescriptionMessage.label: OT Device Description Message
OTDeviceDescriptionMessage.documentation: Describe features, abilities, or performance of system components.

OTDeviceDescriptionMessageEvent.label: OT Device Description Message Event
OTDeviceDescriptionMessageEvent.documentation: Describe features, abilities, or performance of system components.

OTDeviceFirmwareCommand.label: OT Device Firmware Command
OTDeviceFirmwareCommand.documentation: Interact with the software responsible for low-level control of the system.

OTDeviceFirmwareCommandEvent.label: OT Device Firmware Command Event
OTDeviceFirmwareCommandEvent.documentation: Interact with the software responsible for low-level control of the system.

OTDiagnosticsMessage.label: OT Diagnostics Message
OTDiagnosticsMessage.documentation: Relay error, exception, alarm, or log information.

OTDiagnosticsMessageEvent.label: OT Diagnostics Message Event
OTDiagnosticsMessageEvent.documentation: Relay error, exception, alarm, or log information.

OTDisconnectRemoteConnectionCommand.label: OT Disconnect Remote Connection Command
OTDisconnectRemoteConnectionCommand.documentation: The Disconnect Request message is sent to the message receiver to indicate that the transmitter is terminating its TCP socket.

OTDisconnectRemoteConnectionCommandEvent.label: OT Disconnect Remote Connection Command Event
OTDisconnectRemoteConnectionCommandEvent.documentation: The Disconnect Request message is sent to the message receiver to indicate that the transmitter is terminating its TCP socket.

OTDownloadControlProgramCommand.label: OT Download Control Program Command
OTDownloadControlProgramCommand.documentation: Commands a remote device to download a control program.

OTDownloadControlProgramCommandEvent.label: OT Download Control Program Command Event
OTDownloadControlProgramCommandEvent.documentation: Commands a remote device to download a control program.

OTEmbeddedComputer.label: OT Embedded Computer
OTEmbeddedComputer.documentation: A ruggedized computational device, embedded in industrial control systems, designed to handle real-time tasks and environmental stressors common in OT.

OTEngineeringSoftware.label: OT Engineering Software
OTEngineeringSoftware.documentation: Software used in an industrial process to help engineers design, test, and maintain OT. This software enables the programming of OT controllers.

OTEngineeringWorkstation.label: OT Engineering Workstation
OTEngineeringWorkstation.documentation: An Engineering Workstation (EWS) is used to perform various maintenance, configuration, or diagnostics functions for a control system. The EWS will likely require dedicated application software to interface with various devices (e.g., RTUs, PLCs), and may be used to transfer data or files between the control system devices and other networks.

OTErrorMessage.label: OT Error Message
OTErrorMessage.documentation: An anticipated, reproducible defect occurred within the system.

OTErrorMessageEvent.label: OT Error Message Event
OTErrorMessageEvent.documentation: An anticipated, reproducible defect occurred within the system.

OTEstablishRemoteConnectionCommand.label: OT Establish Remote Connection Command
OTEstablishRemoteConnectionCommand.documentation: Used to establish an TCP/IP Connection to the target device.

OTEstablishRemoteConnectionCommandEvent.label: OT Establish Remote Connection Command Event
OTEstablishRemoteConnectionCommandEvent.documentation: Used to establish an TCP/IP Connection to the target device.

OTEvent.label: OT Event
OTEvent.documentation: A discrete occurrence within an operational technology environment that denotes a significant change in state, execution of a command, or transmission of information.

OTExceptionMessage.label: OT Exception Message
OTExceptionMessage.documentation: An unknown or anomalous condition occurred in the system.

OTExceptionMessageEvent.label: OT Exception Message Event
OTExceptionMessageEvent.documentation: An unknown or anomalous condition occurred in the system.

OTHumanMachineInterface.label: OT Human Machine Interface
OTHumanMachineInterface.documentation: Human-Machine Interfaces (HMIs) are systems used by an operator to monitor the real-time status of an operational process and to perform necessary control functions, including the adjustment of device parameters.

OTIOModule.label: OT I/O Module
OTIOModule.documentation: An OT I/O Module is an industrial-grade interface designed for harsh Operational Technology (OT) environments. It reliably connects sensors and actuators to industrial control systems, ensuring precise, real-time data exchange in applications such as SCADA or ICS. Engineered for ruggedness and consistent performance, it can manage analog, digital, or other specialized signal types while enduring demanding conditions.

OTLogicVariable.label: OT Logic Variable
OTLogicVariable.documentation: A variable which directly affects a program running on an OT controller, involving an OT Process.

OTModeSwitch.label: OT Mode Switch
OTModeSwitch.documentation: Keyswitch or mode switch is the mechanism for changing the operating mode of an OT controller or device.

OTModifyControlProgramCommand.label: OT Modify Control Program Command
OTModifyControlProgramCommand.documentation: OT command that adds, removes, or changes, process data on a remote device.

OTModifyControlProgramCommandEvent.label: OT Modify Control Program Command Event
OTModifyControlProgramCommandEvent.documentation: OT command that adds, removes, or changes, process data on a remote device.

OTModifyDeviceConfigurationCommandEvent.label: OT Modify Device Configuration Command Event

OTModifyDeviceOperatingModeCommand.label: OT Modify Device Operating Mode Command
OTModifyDeviceOperatingModeCommand.documentation: Modifies the running state of an application or program on a device.

OTModifyDeviceOperatingModeCommandEvent.label: OT Modify Device Operating Mode Command Event
OTModifyDeviceOperatingModeCommandEvent.documentation: Modifies the running state of an application or program on a device.

OTNetwork.label: OT Network
OTNetwork.documentation: A computer network which connects OT devices.

OTNetworkManagementCommand.label: OT Network Management Command
OTNetworkManagementCommand.documentation: Manage message routing or network connection mechanisms.

OTNetworkManagementCommandEvent.label: OT Network Management Command Event
OTNetworkManagementCommandEvent.documentation: Manage message routing or network connection mechanisms.

OTNetworkTraffic.label: OT Network Traffic
OTNetworkTraffic.documentation: Network traffic generated by operational technology devices, e.g., programmable logic controllers.

OTPauseCommand.label: OT Pause Command
OTPauseCommand.documentation: Commands a device to pause a service/program.

OTPauseCommandEvent.label: OT Pause Command Event
OTPauseCommandEvent.documentation: Commands a device to pause a service/program.

OTPowerSupply.label: OT Power Supply
OTPowerSupply.documentation: An OT power supply is a power supply whose control amplifier is optimized for signal-processing tasks rather than supplying mere steady-state power to a load. It is a self-contained combination of operational amplifiers, power amplifiers, and integral power circuits designed for higher-level operations in industrial or OT contexts.

OTProcessDataCommand.label: OT Process Data Command
OTProcessDataCommand.documentation: Manage data associated with a controlled process.

OTProcessDataCommandEvent.label: OT Process Data Command Event
OTProcessDataCommandEvent.documentation: Manage data associated with a controlled process.

OTProcessDataHistorian.label: OT Process Data Historian
OTProcessDataHistorian.documentation: A system used to collect and store data, including telemetry, events, alerts, and alarms about the operational process and supporting devices.

OTProcessVariable.label: OT Process Variable
OTProcessVariable.documentation: Process variables are the current actual measurement of the physical characteristics of a system. Common process variables include but are not limited to Temperature, Pressure, Level, and Flow.

OTProgramModeCommand.label: OT Program Mode Command
OTProgramModeCommand.documentation: Command that places the controller in a mode capable of reprogramming logic. This may or may not stop the program.

OTProgramModeCommandEvent.label: OT Program Mode Command Event
OTProgramModeCommandEvent.documentation: Command that places the controller in a mode capable of reprogramming logic. This may or may not stop the program.

OTProprietaryMessage.label: OT Proprietary Message
OTProprietaryMessage.documentation: Vendor specific and may not be publicly documented, or values left for device specific configuration.

OTProprietaryMessageEvent.label: OT Proprietary Message Event
OTProprietaryMessageEvent.documentation: Vendor specific and may not be publicly documented, or values left for device specific configuration.

OTProtocolMessage.label: OT Protocol Message
OTProtocolMessage.documentation: Packets generated by an operational technology protocol contain an OT protocol message.

OTReadDeviceConfigurationCommandEvent.label: OT Read Device Configuration Command Event

OTReadFileCommand.label: OT Read File Command
OTReadFileCommand.documentation: Reads data in specified chuncks or the contents of a specified file stored in the file device connected to the PC.

OTReadFileCommandEvent.label: OT Read File Command Event
OTReadFileCommandEvent.documentation: Reads data in specified chuncks or the contents of a specified file stored in the file device connected to the PC.

OTReadValueCommand.label: OT Read Value Command
OTReadValueCommand.documentation: Reads the contents of the specified number of consecutive parameter areawords starting from the specified word.

OTReadValueCommandEvent.label: OT Read Value Command Event
OTReadValueCommandEvent.documentation: Reads the contents of the specified number of consecutive parameter areawords starting from the specified word.

OTRemoteModeCommand.label: OT Remote Mode Command
OTRemoteModeCommand.documentation: Command that places the controller in a mode capable of receiving read/write communication from a networked entity.

OTRemoteModeCommandEvent.label: OT Remote Mode Command Event
OTRemoteModeCommandEvent.documentation: Command that places the controller in a mode capable of receiving read/write communication from a networked entity.

OTRunCommand.label: OT Run Command
OTRunCommand.documentation: Commands a device to start or resume a service/program.

OTRunCommandEvent.label: OT Run Command Event
OTRunCommandEvent.documentation: Commands a device to start or resume a service/program.

OTScanTime.label: OT Scan Time
OTScanTime.documentation: An OT controller system variable that tracks the measured time it takes to read input status, apply logic, and write output values.

OTSecurityCommand.label: OT Security Command
OTSecurityCommand.documentation: Ensure confidentiality, integrity, or availability of system information.

OTSecurityCommandEvent.label: OT Security Command Event
OTSecurityCommandEvent.documentation: Ensure confidentiality, integrity, or availability of system information.

OTSensor.label: OT Sensor
OTSensor.documentation: An OT Sensor is an industrial-grade sensing device engineered for operational technology (OT) environments (e.g. SCADA, ICS). It measures physical variables—such as pressure, temperature, or flow—under demanding conditions, converting them into reliable signals for real-time monitoring and process control loops.

OTStopCommand.label: OT Stop Command
OTStopCommand.documentation: Commands a device to stop a service/program.

OTStopCommandEvent.label: OT Stop Command Event
OTStopCommandEvent.documentation: Commands a device to stop a service/program.

OTTestCommand.label: OT Test Command
OTTestCommand.documentation: Commands a  device to run a program in Test mode.

OTTestCommandEvent.label: OT Test Command Event
OTTestCommandEvent.documentation: Commands a  device to run a program in Test mode.

OTTimeCommand.label: OT Time Command
OTTimeCommand.documentation: Read, set, or calculate timing mechanisms.

OTTimeCommandEvent.label: OT Time Command Event
OTTimeCommandEvent.documentation: Read, set, or calculate timing mechanisms.

OTTransportConfigurationCommand.label: OT Transport Configuration Command
OTTransportConfigurationCommand.documentation: Configure transport settings for a communication channel.

OTTransportConfigurationCommandEvent.label: OT Transport Configuration Command Event
OTTransportConfigurationCommandEvent.documentation: Configure transport settings for a communication channel.

OTVariableAccessRestriction.label: OT Variable Access Restriction
OTVariableAccessRestriction.documentation: Assign read/write access controls on designated registers or data tags to prevent unauthorized writes.

OTWatchdogTimer.label: OT Watchdog Timer
OTWatchdogTimer.documentation: An OT Watchdog Timer is a software-based monitoring mechanism used in operational technology (OT) environments to continuously supervise the execution and responsiveness of critical control applications, devices, or communication links. It operates by requiring periodic “heartbeat” signals or status updates from monitored processes within a defined time window; if these signals are not received on time (indicating a hang, fault, or abnormal delay) the OT Watchdog Timer automatically triggers predefined safety or recovery actions, such as placing equipment in a fail-safe state, restarting services, generating alarms, or initiating controlled shutdowns.

OWL.label: OWL
OWL.documentation: The Web Ontology Language (OWL) is a family of knowledge representation languages for authoring ontologies.

ObjectEviction.label: Object Eviction
ObjectEviction.documentation: Terminate or remove an object from a host machine. This is the broadest class for object eviction.

ObjectFile.label: Object File
ObjectFile.documentation: An object file is a file that contains relocatable machine code.

OffensiveTactic.label: Offensive Tactic
OffensiveTactic.documentation: Per ATT&CK, these are defined as Tactical Goals, not Tactics per se. Many children also fit definition of tactics.  Some are neither tactics or tactical goals really (e.g., Execution, which is a useful grouping, but an action, not really a tactic or technique.

OfficeApplication.label: Office Application
OfficeApplication.documentation: An office application is one that is part of an application suite (e.g., Microsoft Office, Open Office).

OfficeApplicationFile.label: Office Application File
OfficeApplicationFile.documentation: A document file in a format associated with an d3f:OfficeApplication.

OnboardComputer.label: Onboard Computer
OnboardComputer.documentation: A self-contained, embedded computing unit installed within a vehicle or other autonomous platform that executes real-time control, data-handling, and mission-management software. It interfaces directly with the platform's sensors, actuators, and communication links, processes and stores operational data, and issues commands to subsystems, enabling the system to function independently of external computing resources.

One-timePassword.label: One-time Password
One-timePassword.documentation: A one-time password is valid for only one user authentication.

Open-sourceDeveloper.label: Open-source Developer
Open-sourceDeveloper.documentation: An open-source developer contributes to the development, maintenance, or improvement of open-source projects.

OpenFile.label: Open File
OpenFile.documentation: For most file systems, a program initializes access to a file in a file system using the open system call. This allocates resources associated to the file (the file descriptor), and returns a handle that the process will use to refer to that file. In some cases the open is performed by the first access. During the open, the filesystem may allocate memory for buffers, or it may wait until the first operation. Various other errors which may occur during the open include directory update failures, un-permitted multiple connections, media failures, communication link failures and device failures.

OperatingMode.label: Operating Mode
OperatingMode.documentation: An operating mode designates the specific way a system, product, or service functions for a particular task, configuration, or phase of operation

OperatingModeMonitoring.label: Operating Mode Monitoring
OperatingModeMonitoring.documentation: Detects operating modes such as Program, Run, Remote, or Stop.

OperatingModeRestriction.label: Operating Mode Restriction
OperatingModeRestriction.documentation: Restricting unauthorized changes to the operating mode prevents devices from switching into inappropriate or vulnerable states during normal use.

OperatingSystem.label: Operating System
OperatingSystem.documentation: An operating system (OS) is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources and provides common services for computer programs. All computer programs, excluding firmware, require an operating system to function. Time-sharing operating systems schedule tasks for efficient use of the system and may also include accounting software for cost allocation of processor time, mass storage, printing, and other resources.

OperatingSystemClock.label: Operating System Clock
OperatingSystemClock.documentation: An operating system clock is the primary software clock maintained by the operating system, representing the system's current time. It is used for timestamping files, scheduling tasks, and synchronizing processes.

OperatingSystemConfiguration.label: Operating System Configuration
OperatingSystemConfiguration.documentation: Information used to configure the services, parameters, and initial settings for an operating system.

OperatingSystemConfigurationComponent.label: Operating System Configuration Component
OperatingSystemConfigurationComponent.documentation: An component of the overall information necessary for the configuration of an operating system.

OperatingSystemConfigurationFile.label: Operating System Configuration File
OperatingSystemConfigurationFile.documentation: An operating system configuration file is a file used to configure the operating system.

OperatingSystemConfigurationModification.label: Operating System Configuration Modification Event
OperatingSystemConfigurationModification.documentation: An event that alters persistent operating-system configuration resources such as kernel options, registry keys, service definitions, or security policies; affecting system startup, hardware interfaces, or global security enforcement.

OperatingSystemExecutableFile.label: Operating System Executable File
OperatingSystemExecutableFile.documentation: An operating system executable is a critical executable that is part of the operating system, and without which, the operating system may not operate correctly.

OperatingSystemFile.label: Operating System File
OperatingSystemFile.documentation: An operating system file is a file that is part of, or used to store information about, the operating system itself.

OperatingSystemLogFile.label: Operating System Log File
OperatingSystemLogFile.documentation: An operating system log file records events that occur in an operating system.

OperatingSystemMonitoring.label: Operating System Monitoring
OperatingSystemMonitoring.documentation: The operating system software, for D3FEND's purposes, includes the kernel and its process management functions, hardware drivers, initialization or boot logic. It also includes and other key system daemons and their configuration. The monitoring or analysis of these components for unauthorized activity constitute **Operating System Monitoring**.

OperatingSystemPackagingTool.label: Operating System Packaging Tool
OperatingSystemPackagingTool.documentation: A software packaging tool oriented on building a software package for a particular operating system (e.g. rpmbuild.)

OperatingSystemProcess.label: Operating System Process
OperatingSystemProcess.documentation: An operating system process, or system process, is a process running to perform operating system functions.

OperatingSystemSharedLibraryFile.label: Operating System Shared Library File
OperatingSystemSharedLibraryFile.documentation: An operating system shared library file is a shared library file that is part of the operating system and that incorporates common operating system code for use by any application or to provide operating system services.

OperationalActivityMapping.label: Operational Activity Mapping
OperationalActivityMapping.documentation: Operational activity mapping identifies activities of the organization and the organization's suborganizations, groups, roles, and individuals that carry out the activities and then establishes the dependencies of the activities on the systems and people that perform those activities.

OperationalActivityPlan.label: Operational Activity Plan
OperationalActivityPlan.documentation: An activity is a specific behavior representing a set of actions that may be accomplished by an agent.

OperationalDependencyMapping.label: Operational Dependency Mapping
OperationalDependencyMapping.documentation: Operational dependency mapping identifies and models the dependencies of the organization's activities on each other and on the organization's performers (people, systems, and services.)  This may include modeling the higher- and lower-level activities of an organization forming a hierarchy, or layering, of the dependencies in an organization's activities.

OperationalEvent.label: Operational Event
OperationalEvent.documentation: An Operational Event is an action or occurrence within an organization's mission or business operations that happens over a period of time.

OperationalLogicValidation.label: Operational Logic Validation
OperationalLogicValidation.documentation: Validation of variable state in the context of the control logic of the operational application.

OperationalProcessMonitoring.label: Operational Process Monitoring
OperationalProcessMonitoring.documentation: Monitoring physical parameters and operator actions related to an operational environment.

OperationalRiskAssessment.label: Operational Risk Assessment
OperationalRiskAssessment.documentation: Operational risk assessment identifies and models the vulnerabilities of, and risks to, an organization's activities individually and as a whole.

OperationsCenterComputer.label: Operations Center Computer
OperationsCenterComputer.documentation: Mainframe computers or mainframes (colloquially referred to as "big iron") are computers used primarily by large organizations for critical applications; bulk data processing, such as census, industry and consumer statistics, and enterprise resource planning; and transaction processing. They are larger and have more processing power than some other classes of computers: minicomputers, servers, workstations, and personal computers.

OpticalDiscImage.label: Optical Disc Image
OpticalDiscImage.documentation: An optical disc image (or ISO image, from the ISO 9660 file system used with CD-ROM media) is a disk image that contains everything that would be written to an optical disc, disk sector by disc sector, including the optical disc file system.

OpticalModem.label: Optical Modem
OpticalModem.documentation: A modem that connects to a fiber optic network is known as an optical network terminal (ONT) or optical network unit (ONU). These are commonly used in fiber to the home installations, installed inside or outside a house to convert the optical medium to a copper Ethernet interface, after which a router or gateway is often installed to perform authentication, routing, NAT, and other typical consumer internet functions, in addition to "triple play" features such as telephony and television service.

OrchestrationController.label: Orchestration Controller
OrchestrationController.documentation: An orchestration server provides orchestration services that automate the configuration, coordination, and management of computer systems and software.

OrchestrationServer.label: Orchestration Server
OrchestrationServer.documentation: A d3f:Server which is involved with the orchestration of workloads or the execution of orchestrated workloads.

OrchestrationWorker.label: Orchestration Worker
OrchestrationWorker.documentation: A d3f:Server which receives commands from a d3f:OrchestrationController to execute workloads.

Organization.label: Organization
Organization.documentation: An organization with a defined mission/goal and a defined boundary, using systems to execute that mission, and with responsibility for managing its own risks and performance. An enterprise may consist of all or some of the following business aspects: acquisition, program management, human resources, financial management, security, and systems, information and mission management

OrganizationMapping.label: Organization Mapping
OrganizationMapping.documentation: Organization mapping identifies and models the people, roles, and groups with an organization and the relations between them.

OutboundInternetDNSLookupTraffic.label: Outbound Internet DNS Lookup Traffic
OutboundInternetDNSLookupTraffic.documentation: Outbound internet DNS lookup traffic is network traffic using the DNS protocol on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network.

OutboundInternetEncryptedRemoteTerminalT.label: Outbound Internet Encrypted Remote Terminal Traffic
OutboundInternetEncryptedRemoteTerminalT.documentation: Outbound internet encrypted remote terminal traffic is encrypted network traffic for a standard remote terminal protocol on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network.

OutboundInternetEncryptedTraffic.label: Outbound Internet Encrypted Traffic
OutboundInternetEncryptedTraffic.documentation: Outbound internet encrypted traffic is encrypted network traffic on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network.

OutboundInternetEncryptedWebTraffic.label: Outbound Internet Encrypted Web Traffic
OutboundInternetEncryptedWebTraffic.documentation: Outbound internet encrypted web traffic is network traffic using a standard web protocol on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network.

OutboundInternetFileTransferTraffic.label: Outbound Internet File Transfer Traffic
OutboundInternetFileTransferTraffic.documentation: Outbound internet file transfer traffic is file transfer traffic that is: (a) on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network, and (b) using a standard file transfer protocol.

OutboundInternetMailTraffic.label: Outbound Internet Mail Traffic
OutboundInternetMailTraffic.documentation: Outbound internet DNS lookup traffic is network traffic using a standard email protocol on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network.

OutboundInternetNetworkTraffic.label: Outbound Internet Network Traffic
OutboundInternetNetworkTraffic.documentation: Outbound internet network traffic is network traffic on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network.

OutboundInternetRPCTraffic.label: Outbound Internet RPC Traffic
OutboundInternetRPCTraffic.documentation: Outbound internet RPC traffic is RPC traffic that is: (a) on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network, and (b) using a standard RPC protocol.

OutboundInternetWebTraffic.label: Outbound Internet Web Traffic
OutboundInternetWebTraffic.documentation: Outbound internet web traffic is network traffic that is: (a) on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network, and (b) using a standard web protocol.

OutboundNetworkTraffic.label: Outbound Network Traffic
OutboundNetworkTraffic.documentation: Outbound traffic is network traffic originating from a host of interest (client), to another host (server).

OutboundTrafficFiltering.label: Outbound Traffic Filtering
OutboundTrafficFiltering.documentation: Restricting network traffic originating from a private host or enclave destined towards untrusted networks.

OutputDevice.label: Output Device
OutputDevice.documentation: An output device is any piece of computer hardware equipment which converts information into human-readable form. It can be text, graphics, tactile, audio, and video. Some of the output devices are Visual Display Units (VDU) i.e. a Monitor, Printer, Graphic Output devices, Plotters, Speakers etc. A new type of Output device is been developed these days, known as Speech synthesizer, a mechanism attached to the computer which produces verbal output sounding almost like human speeches.

OutputDeviceEvent.label: Output Device Event
OutputDeviceEvent.documentation: An event describing the activity or state of output devices, including sound cards, display adapters, or media controllers. These events relate to audio, video, or graphics functionality.

PER-0001.label: Memory Compromise - SPARTA
PER-0001.documentation: The adversary arranges for malicious content to survive resets and mode changes by targeting memories and execution paths that initialize the system. Candidates include boot ROM handoff vectors, first/second-stage loaders, non-volatile images (flash/EEPROM), “golden” fallback partitions, configuration words/fuses, and RAM regions reconstructed at start-up from stored files or tables. Persistence may also ride auto-run mechanisms, init scripts, procedure engines, stored command sequences, or event hooks that execute on boot, safe-mode entry/exit, time triggers, or receipt of specific telemetry/commands. Variants keep the core payload only in RAM but ensure it is reloaded after every restart by patching copy-on-boot routines, altering file catalogs, or modifying table loaders so the same bytes are restored. The common thread is control of where the spacecraft looks for what to run next, so unauthorized logic is reinstated whenever the system resets or transitions modes.

PER-0002.label: Backdoor - SPARTA
PER-0002.documentation: A backdoor is a covert access path that bypasses normal authentication, authorization, or operational checks so the attacker can reenter the system on demand. Backdoors may be preexisting (undocumented service modes, maintenance accounts, debug features) or introduced by the adversary during development, integration, or on-orbit updates. Triggers range from “magic” opcodes and timetags to specific geometry/time conditions, counters, or data patterns embedded in routine traffic. The access they provide varies from expanded command sets and relaxed rate/size limits to alternate communications profiles and hidden file/parameter interfaces. Well-crafted backdoors blend with nominal behavior, appearing as ordinary operations while quietly accepting instructions that other paths would reject, thereby sustaining the attacker’s foothold across passes, resets, and operator handovers.

PER-0002.01.label: Hardware Backdoor - SPARTA
PER-0002.01.documentation: Hardware backdoors leverage properties of the physical design to provide durable, low-visibility reentry. Examples include enabled test/scan chains, manufacturing or boot-strap modes invoked by pins or registers, persistent debug interfaces (JTAG/SWD/UART), undocumented device commands, and logic inserted in FPGA/ASIC designs that activates under specific stimuli. Because these mechanisms sit below or beside flight software, they can grant direct access to buses, memories, or peripheral control even when higher layers appear healthy. Triggers may be electrical (pin states, voltage/clock sequences), protocol-level (special patterns on an instrument link), or environmental/temporal (particular temperature ranges, timing offsets). Once on orbit, such pathways are difficult to remove or reconfigure, allowing the attacker to persist by reusing the same physical entry points whenever conditions are met.

PER-0002.02.label: Software Backdoor - SPARTA
PER-0002.02.documentation: Software backdoors are code paths intentionally crafted or later inserted to provide privileged functionality on cue. In flight contexts, they appear as hidden command handlers, alternate authentication checks, special user/role constructs, or procedure/script hooks that accept nonpublic inputs. They can be embedded in flight applications, separation kernels or drivers, gateway processors that translate bus/payload traffic, or update/loader utilities that handle tables and images. SDR configurations offer another avenue: non-public waveforms, subcarriers, or framing profiles that, when selected, expose a private command channel. Activation is often conditional, specific timetags, geometry, message sequences, or file names, to keep the feature dormant during routine testing and operations. Once present, the backdoor provides a repeatable way to execute commands or modify state without traversing the standard control surfaces, sustaining the adversary’s access over time.

PER-0003.label: Ground System Presence - SPARTA
PER-0003.documentation: The adversary maintains long-lived access by residing within mission ground infrastructure that already has end-to-end reach to the spacecraft. Persistence can exist in operator workstations and mission control software, schedulers/orchestrators, station control (antenna/mount, modem/baseband), automation scripts and procedure libraries, identity and ticketing systems, and cloud-hosted mission services. With this foothold, the actor can repeatedly queue commands, updates, or file transfers during routine passes; mirror legitimate operator behavior to blend in; and refresh their tooling as software is upgraded. Presence on the ground also supports durable reconnaissance (pass plans, dictionaries, key/counter states) and continuous staging so each window to the vehicle can be exploited without re-establishing access.

PER-0004.label: Replace Cryptographic Keys - SPARTA
PER-0004.documentation: The adversary cements control by changing the cryptographic material the spacecraft uses to authenticate or protect links and updates. Targets include uplink authentication keys and counters, link-encryption/session keys and key-encryption keys (KEKs), key identifiers/selectors, and algorithm profiles. Using authorized rekey commands or key-loading procedures, often designed for over-the-air use, the attacker installs new values in non-volatile storage and updates selectors so subsequent traffic must use the attacker’s keys to be accepted. Variants desynchronize anti-replay by advancing counters or switching epochs, or strand operators by flipping profiles to a mode for which only the adversary holds parameters. Once replaced, the new material persists across resets and mode changes, turning the spacecraft into a node that recognizes the adversary’s channel while rejecting former controllers.

PER-0005.label: Credentialed Persistence - SPARTA
PER-0005.documentation: Threat actors may acquire or leverage valid credentials to maintain persistent access to a spacecraft or its supporting command and control (C2) systems. These credentials may include system service accounts, user accounts, maintenance access credentials, cryptographic keys, or other authentication mechanisms that enable continued entry without triggering access alarms. By operating with legitimate credentials, adversaries can sustain access over extended periods, evade detection, and facilitate follow-on tactics such as command execution, data exfiltration, or lateral movement. Credentialed persistence is particularly effective in environments lacking strong credential lifecycle management, segmentation, or monitoring allowing threat actors to exploit trusted pathways while remaining embedded in mission operations.

POSIXSymbolicLink.label: POSIX Symbolic Link
POSIXSymbolicLink.documentation: A POSIX-compliant symbolic link.  These are often fast symbolic links, but need not be.

PackageURL.label: Package URL
PackageURL.documentation: A package URL, or purl, is a URL used to identify a software package in a mostly universal and uniform way across programming languages, package managers, packaging conventions, tools, APIs and databases.

PacketCaptureFile.label: Packet Capture File
PacketCaptureFile.documentation: A file which contains raw representations of collected packets.

PacketLog.label: Packet Log
PacketLog.documentation: A log of all the network packet data captured from a network by a network sensor (i.e., packet analyzer),

Page.label: Page
Page.documentation: A page, memory page, logical page, or virtual page is a fixed-length contiguous block of virtual memory, described by a single entry in the page table. It is the smallest unit of data for memory management in a virtual memory operating system.

PageFrame.label: Page Frame
PageFrame.documentation: A page frame is the smallest fixed-length contiguous block of physical memory into which memory pages are mapped by the operating system.

PageTable.label: Page Table
PageTable.documentation: A page table  is the data structure used by the MMU in a virtual memory computer system  to store the mapping between virtual addresses (virtual pages) and physical addresses (page frames).

Parameter-basedTransferLearning.label: Parameter-based Transfer Learning
Parameter-basedTransferLearning.documentation: The idea behind parameter-based methods is that a well-trained model on the source domain has learned a well-defined structure, and if two tasks are related, this structure can be transferred to the target model.

ParametricTests.label: Parametric Tests
ParametricTests.documentation: A parametric test relies upon the assumption that the data you want to test is (or approximately is) normally distributed.

ParentProcess.label: Parent Process
ParentProcess.documentation: In computing, a parent process is a process that has created one or more child processes.

PartialMatching.label: Partial Matching
PartialMatching.documentation: Partial string pattern matching is a special case of string pattern matching where one seeks to find a pattern within a larger string (text). It allows for the detection of patterns that occur as substrings or partial segments within the full string, rather than requiring an exact match across the entire string.

ParticleRadiationHardening.label: Particle Radiation Hardening
ParticleRadiationHardening.documentation: The application of material, process, layout, or circuit-level design measures to electronic systems and components to reduce susceptibility to total ionizing dose degradation and single-event effects caused by ionizing particles such as protons, heavy ions, neutrons, or electrons.

Partition.label: Partition
Partition.documentation: A partition is a region on secondary storage device created so that the region can be managed by itself; separate from any other regions (partitions) on that secondary storage device. Creating partitions is typically the first step of preparing a newly installed storage device, before any file system is created. The device stores the information about the partitions' locations and sizes in an area known as the partition table that the operating system reads before any other part of the disk. Each partition then appears to the operating system as a distinct "logical" storage device that uses part of the actual device. System administrators use a program called a partition editor to create, resize, delete, and manipulate the partitions. Partitioning allows the use of different filesystems to be installed for different kinds of files. Separating user data from system data can prevent the system partition from becoming full and rendering the system unusable. Partitioning can also make backing up easier. [Definition adapted as generalization from definition of disk partitioning and distinct from in-memory partitions.]

PartitionTable.label: Partition Table
PartitionTable.documentation: A partition is a fixed-size subset of a storage device which is treated as a unit by the operating system. A partition table is a table maintained on the storage device by the operating system describing the partitions on that device. The terms partition table and partition map are most commonly associated with the MBR partition table of a Master Boot Record (MBR) in IBM PC compatibles, but it may be used generically to refer to other "formats" that divide a disk drive into partitions, such as: GUID Partition Table (GPT), Apple partition map (APM), or BSD disklabel.

PassiveCertificateAnalysis.label: Passive Certificate Analysis
PassiveCertificateAnalysis.documentation: Collecting host certificates from network traffic or other passive sources like a certificate transparency log and analyzing them for unauthorized activity.

PassiveLogicalLinkMapping.label: Passive Logical Link Mapping
PassiveLogicalLinkMapping.documentation: Passive logical link mapping only listens to network traffic as a means to map the the whole data link layer, where the links represent logical data flows rather than physical connections.

Password.label: Password
Password.documentation: A password, sometimes called a passcode, is a memorized secret, typically a string of characters, usually used to confirm the identity of a user. Using the terminology of the NIST Digital Identity Guidelines, the secret is memorized by a party called the claimant while the party verifying the identity of the claimant is called the verifier. When the claimant successfully demonstrates knowledge of the password to the verifier through an established authentication protocol, the verifier is able to infer the claimant's identity.

PasswordAuthentication.label: Password Authentication
PasswordAuthentication.documentation: Password authentication is a security mechanism used to verify the identity of a user or entity attempting to access a system or resource by requiring the input of a secret string of characters, known as a password, that is associated with the user or entity.

PasswordDatabase.label: Password Database
PasswordDatabase.documentation: A password database is a database that holds passwords for user accounts and is usually encrypted (i.e.., the passwords are hashed). Password databases are found supporting system services (such as SAM) or part of user applications such as password managers.

PasswordFile.label: Password File
PasswordFile.documentation: Simple form of password database held in a single file (e.g., /etc/password)

PasswordManager.label: Password Manager
PasswordManager.documentation: A password manager is a software application or hardware that helps a user store and organize passwords. Password managers usually store passwords encrypted, requiring the user to create a master password: a single, ideally very strong password which grants the user access to their entire password database. Some password managers store passwords on the user's computer (called offline password managers), whereas others store data in the provider's cloud (often called online password managers). However offline password managers also offer data storage in the user's own cloud accounts rather than the provider's cloud. While the core functionality of a password manager is to securely store large collections of passwords, many provide additional features such as form filling and password generation.

PasswordRotation.label: Password Rotation
PasswordRotation.documentation: Password rotation is a security policy that mandates the periodic change of user account passwords to mitigate the risk of unauthorized access due to compromised credentials.

PasswordStore.label: Password Store
PasswordStore.documentation: A user repository of account passwords, often accessed via a password manager.

PatternMatching.label: Pattern Matching
PatternMatching.documentation: Pattern matching is the act of checking a given sequence of tokens for the presence of the constituents of some pattern.

PerHostDownload-UploadRatioAnalysis.label: Per Host Download-Upload Ratio Analysis
PerHostDownload-UploadRatioAnalysis.documentation: Detecting anomalies that indicate malicious activity by comparing the amount of data downloaded versus data uploaded by a host.

PeripheralDeviceEvent.label: Peripheral Device Event
PeripheralDeviceEvent.documentation: An event involving external or auxiliary devices, such as USB drives, Thunderbolt peripherals, or Bluetooth devices. Peripheral events provide visibility into resource availability and potential unauthorized access.

PeripheralFirmware.label: Peripheral Firmware
PeripheralFirmware.documentation: Firmware that is installed on computer peripheral devices.

PeripheralHubFirmware.label: Peripheral Hub Firmware
PeripheralHubFirmware.documentation: Firmware that is installed on peripheral hub device such as a USB or Firewire hub.

PermissionGrantingEvent.label: Permission Granting Event
PermissionGrantingEvent.documentation: An administrative event where authorization is given, allowing a subject to perform specific operations on a protected resource, effectuating a policy decision to allow access rights.

PermissionRevokingEvent.label: Permission Revoking Event
PermissionRevokingEvent.documentation: An administrative event entailing the withdrawal of previously granted access rights, reconfiguring permissions to prevent a subject from performing specific actions on a resource, in accordance with updated access policies.

PersistenceTechnique.label: Persistence Technique
PersistenceTechnique.documentation: The adversary is trying to maintain their foothold.

Person.label: Person
Person.documentation: A person is a human being.

PersonalComputer.label: Personal Computer
PersonalComputer.documentation: A personal computer (PC) is a multi-purpose computer whose size, capabilities, and price make it feasible for individual use. Personal computers are intended to be operated directly by an end user, rather than by a computer expert or technician. Unlike large, costly minicomputers and mainframes, time-sharing by many people at the same time is not used with personal computers. PCs have in practice become powerful enough that they may be shared by multiple users at any given time, though this is not common practice nor the primary purpose of a PC.

Perturbation-basedLearning.label: Perturbation-based Learning
Perturbation-basedLearning.documentation: Perturbation based methods are proposed under the smoothness assumption, which indicates that two data points close to each other in feature space are likely to have the same label.

PhiCoefficient.label: Phi Coefficient
PhiCoefficient.documentation: The phi coefficient (or mean square contingency coefficient is a measure of association for two binary variables.

PhysicalAccessAlarmEvent.label: Physical Access Alarm Event
PhysicalAccessAlarmEvent.documentation: An event occuring when a physical threshold is crossed.

PhysicalAccessMediation.label: Physical Access Mediation
PhysicalAccessMediation.documentation: Physical access mediation is the process of granting or denying specific requests to enter specific physical facilities (e.g., Federal buildings, military establishments, border crossing entrances.)

PhysicalAccessMonitoring.label: Physical Access Monitoring
PhysicalAccessMonitoring.documentation: Monitoring the physical access of a specified environment through detection, recording, reviewing, and logging of who/what enters and exists areas.

PhysicalAddress.label: Physical Address
PhysicalAddress.documentation: In a computer supporting virtual memory, the term physical address is used mostly to differentiate from a virtual address. In particular, in computers utilizing a memory management unit(MMU) to translate memory addresses, the virtual and physical addresses refer to an address before and after translation performed by the MMU, respectively.

PhysicalAttacker.label: Physical Attacker
PhysicalAttacker.documentation: An attacker who is physically close enough to interact with the system directly, such as through physical access to devices.

PhysicalDataDiode.label: Physical Data Diode
PhysicalDataDiode.documentation: A device that physically enforces one-way (unidirectional) network communication.

PhysicalEnclosureHardening.label: Physical Enclosure Hardening
PhysicalEnclosureHardening.documentation: Physical changes to a computer enclosure which reduce the ability for agents or the environment to affect the contained computer system.

PhysicalKey.label: Physical Key
PhysicalKey.documentation: A physical key is used to operate a lock, typically metal, designed with specific markers that match the internal mechanism of a lock, allowing it to rotate the lock when inserted.

PhysicalKeyLock.label: Physical Key Lock
PhysicalKeyLock.documentation: A mechanical locking device for securing moveable portions of physical barriers (e.g., doors, gates, drawers) in a secured position.

PhysicalLink.label: Physical Link
PhysicalLink.documentation:
A physical link is a dedicated connection for communication that uses some physical media (electrical, electromagnetic, optical, to include clear spaces or vacuums.)  A physical link represents only a single hop (link) in any larger communcations path, circuit, or network.

NOTE: not synonymous with data link as a data link can be over a telecommunications circuit, which may be a virtual circuit composed of multiple phyical links.

PhysicalLinkConnectEvent.label: Physical Link Connect Event
PhysicalLinkConnectEvent.documentation: The medium is attached or the port is enabled, establishing electrical or optical continuity so that link negotiation can begin.

PhysicalLinkDisableEvent.label: Physical Link Disable Event
PhysicalLinkDisableEvent.documentation: An administrator issues a shutdown or disable command, forcing the link out of service regardless of signal status.

PhysicalLinkDisconnectEvent.label: Physical Link Disconnect Event
PhysicalLinkDisconnectEvent.documentation: The transmission medium is removed or power is cut, physically breaking the path between the two interfaces.

PhysicalLinkDownEvent.label: Physical Link Down Event
PhysicalLinkDownEvent.documentation: Carrier or negotiation is lost, or the port is shut, rendering the link non-operational while the medium remains connected.

PhysicalLinkErrorDisableEvent.label: Physical Link Error Disable Event
PhysicalLinkErrorDisableEvent.documentation: The device automatically disables the link in response to fault conditions such as excessive faults or signal degradation.

PhysicalLinkEvent.label: Physical Link Event
PhysicalLinkEvent.documentation: A discrete event that changes either the presence of the transmission medium or the operational state of a single-hop layer-1 link between two network nodes.

PhysicalLinkMapping.label: Physical Link Mapping
PhysicalLinkMapping.documentation: Physical link mapping identifies and models the link connectivity of the network devices within a physical network.

PhysicalLinkUpEvent.label: Physical Link Up Event
PhysicalLinkUpEvent.documentation: Auto-negotiation and signal detection complete; carrier is present and the link can forward frames.

PhysicalLocation.label: Physical Location
PhysicalLocation.documentation: The terms location  [here, a physical location] and place in geography are used to identify a point or an area on the Earth's surface or elsewhere. The term location generally implies a higher degree of certainty than place, which often indicates an entity with an ambiguous boundary, relying more on human or social attributes of place identity and sense of place than on geometry. The distinction between space and place is considered a central concern of geography, and has been addressed by scholars such as Yi-Fu Tuan and John Agnew.

PhysicalLock.label: Physical Lock
PhysicalLock.documentation: A lock is a mechanical latching device for securing moveable portions of physical barriers in a secured position.

PhysicalLocking.label: Physical Locking
PhysicalLocking.documentation: Employ a mechanical locking device for securing moveable portions of physical barriers (e.g., doors, gates, drawers) in a secured position.

Pipe.label: Pipe
Pipe.documentation: In Unix-like computer operating systems, a pipeline is a mechanism for inter-process communication using message passing.  In the strictest sense, a pipe is a single segment of a pipeline, allowing one process to pass information forward to another.  Network pipes allow processes on different hosts to interact.

Pix2Pix.label: Pix2Pix
Pix2Pix.documentation: Pix2Pix is based on condtional GAN architecture and are trained on paired set of images or scenes from two domains to be used for translation.

PlatformHardening.label: Platform Hardening
PlatformHardening.documentation:
Hardening components of a Platform with the intention of making them more difficult to exploit.

Platforms includes components such as:
* BIOS UEFI Subsystems
* Hardware security devices such as Trusted Platform Modules
* Boot process logic or code
* Kernel software components

PlatformMonitoring.label: Platform Monitoring
PlatformMonitoring.documentation: Monitoring platform components such as operating systems software, hardware devices, or firmware.

PlatformUptime.label: Platform Uptime
PlatformUptime.documentation: A variable that notes the amount of time a platform has been running since its last power cycle or reset.

PlatformUptimeMonitoring.label: Platform Uptime Monitoring
PlatformUptimeMonitoring.documentation: Monitor the amount of time since the last power cycle or restart.

Point-biserialCorrelationCoefficient.label: Point-biserial Correlation Coefficient
Point-biserialCorrelationCoefficient.documentation: The point biserial correlation coefficient (rpb) is a correlation coefficient used when one variable (e.g. Y) is dichotomous; Y can either be "naturally" dichotomous, like whether a coin lands heads or tails, or an artificially dichotomized variable.

PointEstimation.label: Point Estimation
PointEstimation.documentation: A point estimation is a single value that estimates the parameter. Point estimates are single values calculated from the sample

Pointer.label: Pointer
Pointer.documentation: In computer science, a pointer is a programming language object, whose value refers to (or "points to") another value stored elsewhere in the computer memory using its memory address. A pointer references a location in memory, and obtaining the value stored at that location is known as dereferencing the pointer. As an analogy, a page number in a book's index could be considered a pointer to the corresponding page; dereferencing such a pointer would be done by flipping to the page with the given page number.

PointerAuthentication.label: Pointer Authentication
PointerAuthentication.documentation: Comparing the cryptographic hash or derivative of a pointer's value to an expected value.

PointerDereferencingFunction.label: Pointer Dereferencing Function
PointerDereferencingFunction.documentation: A function which has an operation which dereferences a pointer.

PointerValidation.label: Pointer Validation
PointerValidation.documentation: Ensuring that a pointer variable has the required properties for use.

PolicyGradient.label: Policy Gradient
PolicyGradient.documentation: The objective of a Reinforcement Learning Policy Gradient agent is to maximize the “expected” reward when following a policy

PowerAndThermalDeviceEvent.label: Power and Thermal Device Event
PowerAndThermalDeviceEvent.documentation: An event involving power supplies, batteries, or thermal management devices. These events represent changes in power states, temperature thresholds, or cooling system activity.

PowerShellProfileScript.label: PowerShell Profile Script
PowerShellProfileScript.documentation: A PowerShell profile script is a script that runs when PowerShell starts and can be used as a logon script to customize user environments.

PowerSupply.label: Power Supply
PowerSupply.documentation: A power supply is an electrical device or module that converts and regulates energy from a source (e.g., the power grid or batteries) to an appropriate voltage, current, and frequency for one or more loads. It may stand alone or be integrated into its host appliance, often providing overcurrent protection, voltage regulation, or power conditioning for safe, stable operation.

PreAuthenticationEvent.label: Pre-Authentication Event
PreAuthenticationEvent.documentation: An event representing preparatory steps or processes conducted prior to the primary authentication operation. Pre-authentication often involves initial protocol exchanges, cryptographic challenges, or the validation of supplemental factors (e.g., pre-shared keys) to ensure the readiness and security of the authentication workflow.

PredicateLogic.label: Predicate Logic
PredicateLogic.documentation: Predicate logic is is collection of formal systems used in mathematics, philosophy, linguistics, and computer science. First-order logic and Higher-order logic both incorporate predicate logic.

PrimaryStorage.label: Primary Storage
PrimaryStorage.documentation: Primary memory of a computer is memory that is wired directly to the processor, consisting of RAM and possibly ROM.  These terms are used in contrast to mass storage devices and cache memory (although we may note that when a program accesses main memory, it is often actually interacting with a cache).

PrincipalComponentAnalysis.label: Principal Component Analysis
PrincipalComponentAnalysis.documentation: Principal components analysis (PCA) creates a new set of orthogonal variables that contain the same information as the original set. It rotates the axes of variation to give a new set of orthogonal axes, ordered so that they summarize decreasing proportions of the variation.

PrincipalComponentsAnalysis.label: Principal Components Analysis
PrincipalComponentsAnalysis.documentation: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a statistic-based method of identifying patterns in a large dataset while increasing interpretability and preserving information.

PrintServer.label: Print Server
PrintServer.documentation: A print server, or printer server, is a device that connects printers to client computers over a network. It accepts print jobs from the computers and sends the jobs to the appropriate printers, queuing the jobs locally to accommodate the fact that work may arrive more quickly than the printer can actually handle.

PrivateKey.label: Private Key
PrivateKey.documentation: A private key can be used to decrypt messages encrypted using the corresponding public key, or used to sign a message that can be authenticated with the corresponding public key.

PrivilegeEscalationTechnique.label: Privilege Escalation Technique
PrivilegeEscalationTechnique.documentation: The adversary is trying to gain higher-level permissions.

PrivilegedUserAccount.label: Privileged User Account
PrivilegedUserAccount.documentation: A privileged account is a user account that has more privileges than ordinary users. Privileged accounts might, for example, be able to install or remove software, upgrade the operating system, or modify system or application configurations. They might also have access to files that are not normally accessible to standard users. Typical examples are root and administrator accounts. But there also service accounts, system accounts, etc. Privileged accounts are especially powerful, and should be monitored especially closely.

ProbabilisticLogic.label: Probabilistic Logic
ProbabilisticLogic.documentation: Probabilistic logic extends traditional logic truth tables with probabilistic expressions.

Process.label: Process
Process.documentation: A process is an instance of a computer program that is being executed. It contains the program code and its current activity. Depending on the operating system (OS), a process may be made up of multiple threads of execution that execute instructions concurrently. A computer program is a passive collection of instructions, while a process is the actual execution of those instructions. Several processes may be associated with the same program; for example, opening up several instances of the same program often means more than one process is being executed.

ProcessAccessEvent.label: Process Access Event
ProcessAccessEvent.documentation: An event where one process interacts with another, such as reading memory, inspecting state, or altering behavior.

ProcessAnalysis.label: Process Analysis
ProcessAnalysis.documentation: Process Analysis consists of observing a running application process and analyzing it to watch for certain behaviors or conditions which may indicate adversary activity. Analysis can occur inside of the process or through a third-party monitoring application. Examples include monitoring system and privileged calls, monitoring process initiation chains, and memory boundary allocations.

ProcessCodeSegment.label: Process Code Segment
ProcessCodeSegment.documentation: A process code segment, also known as a text segment or simply as text, is a portion of the program's virtual address space that contains executable instructions and corresponds to the loaded image code segment. Includes additional sections such as an import table.

ProcessCodeSegmentVerification.label: Process Code Segment Verification
ProcessCodeSegmentVerification.documentation: Comparing the "text" or "code" memory segments to a source of truth.

ProcessCreationEvent.label: Process Creation Event
ProcessCreationEvent.documentation: An event where a new process is spawned, initializing its execution context and resource allocation.

ProcessDataSegment.label: Process Data Segment
ProcessDataSegment.documentation: A process data segment, is a portion of the program's virtual address space that contains executable instructions and corresponds to the loaded image data segment.

ProcessEnvironmentVariable.label: Process Environment Variable
ProcessEnvironmentVariable.documentation: An environment variable is a dynamic-named value that can affect the way running processes will behave on a computer. They are part of the environment in which a process runs.

ProcessEvent.label: Process Event
ProcessEvent.documentation: An event capturing lifecycle transitions, interactions, or activities of computer processes, including their creation, termination, and inter-process communication.

ProcessEviction.label: Process Eviction
ProcessEviction.documentation: Process eviction techniques terminate or remove running process.

ProcessImage.label: Process Image
ProcessImage.documentation: A process image is a copy of a given process's state at a given point in time. It is often used to create persistence within an otherwise volatile system.

ProcessLineageAnalysis.label: Process Lineage Analysis
ProcessLineageAnalysis.documentation: Identification of suspicious processes executing on an end-point device by examining the ancestry and siblings of a process, and the associated metadata of each node on the tree, such as process execution, duration, and order relative to siblings and ancestors.

ProcessSegment.label: Process Segment
ProcessSegment.documentation: Process segments are distinct partitions of the memory space of a running process.  Heap, data, code, and stack segments are examples of process segments.

ProcessSegmentExecutionPrevention.label: Process Segment Execution Prevention
ProcessSegmentExecutionPrevention.documentation: Preventing execution of any address in a memory region other than the code segment.

ProcessSelf-ModificationDetection.label: Process Self-Modification Detection
ProcessSelf-ModificationDetection.documentation: Detects processes that modify, change, or replace their own code at runtime.

ProcessSetUserIDEvent.label: Process Set User ID Event
ProcessSetUserIDEvent.documentation: An event where a process changes or adopts a specific user identity, modifying its access privileges or operational context.

ProcessSpawnAnalysis.label: Process Spawn Analysis
ProcessSpawnAnalysis.documentation: Analyzing spawn arguments or attributes of a process to detect processes that are unauthorized.

ProcessStartFunction.label: Process Start Function
ProcessStartFunction.documentation: A function creates a new computer process, usually by invoking a create process system call.

ProcessSuspension.label: Process Suspension
ProcessSuspension.documentation: Suspending a running process on a computer system.

ProcessTermination.label: Process Termination
ProcessTermination.documentation: Terminating a running application process on a computer system.

ProcessTerminationEvent.label: Process Termination Event
ProcessTerminationEvent.documentation: An event marking the cessation of a process, including resource deallocation and cleanup, either due to normal completion or abnormal termination.

ProcessTree.label: Process Tree
ProcessTree.documentation: A process tree is a tree structure representation of parent-child relationships established via process spawn operations.

Processor.label: Processor
Processor.documentation: A processor is a hardware component or integrated circuit that performs computations, executes instructions, and processes data to carry out tasks within a computing system.

ProcessorComponent.label: Processor Component
ProcessorComponent.documentation: A Processor Component is a functional subunit or module within a processor that performs specific tasks to support the processor's overall operation.

ProcessorRegister.label: Processor Register
ProcessorRegister.documentation: A processor register is a quickly accessible location available to a computer's processor. Registers usually consist of a small amount of fast storage, although some registers have specific hardware functions, and may be read-only or write-only.

ProductDeveloper.label: Product Developer
ProductDeveloper.documentation: A product developer intentionally designs, creates, or improves products, which may include physical goods, software, or other outputs.

ProgressivelyGrowingGAN.label: Progressively Growing GAN
ProgressivelyGrowingGAN.documentation: Progressive Growing GAN (ProGAN) is an extension to the GAN training process that allows for the stable training of generator models that can output large high-quality images.

ProjectedClustering.label: Projected Clustering
ProjectedClustering.documentation: Projected clustering is a dimension reduction subspace clustering method.

Projection-basedClustering.label: Projection-based Clustering
Projection-basedClustering.documentation: Projection Based Clustering is a clustering framework based on a chosen projection method and projection method a parameter-free high-dimensional data visualization technique.

Prolog.label: Prolog
Prolog.documentation: Prolog has its roots in first-order logic, a formal logic, and unlike many other programming languages.

PropertyListFile.label: Property List File
PropertyListFile.documentation: In the OS X, iOS, NeXTSTEP, and GNUstep programming frameworks, property list files are files that store serialized objects. Property list files use the filename extension .plist, and thus are often referred to as p-list files. Property list files are often used to store a user's settings. They are also used to store information about bundles and applications, a task served by the resource fork in the old Mac OS.

PropositionalLogic.label: Propositional Logic
PropositionalLogic.documentation: Propositional logic deals with statements (i.e., propositions, which can be true or false) and relations between propositions, including the construction of arguments based on them.

ProtocolMetadataAnomalyDetection.label: Protocol Metadata Anomaly Detection
ProtocolMetadataAnomalyDetection.documentation: Collecting network communication protocol metadata and identifying statistical outliers.

Provider.label: Provider
Provider.documentation: Providers are entities that intentionally offer, supply, or facilitate goods, services, or resources through actions of their agents.

ProximitySensor.label: Proximity Sensor
ProximitySensor.documentation: A sensor able to detect the presence of nearby objects without any physical contact.

ProximitySensorMonitoring.label: Proximity Sensor Monitoring
ProximitySensorMonitoring.documentation: Monitoring events from proximity sensors that indicate a credential or tagged asset is within the sensor’s read range or a defined zone. Common enabling technologies include RFID, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), and Ultra-Wideband (UWB).

Proxy-basedWebServerAccessMediation.label: Proxy-based Web Server Access Mediation
Proxy-basedWebServerAccessMediation.documentation: Proxy-based web server access mediation focuses on the regulation of web server access through intermediary proxy servers.

ProxyServer.label: Proxy Server
ProxyServer.documentation: In computer networking, a proxy server is a server application or appliance that acts as an intermediary for requests from clients seeking resources from servers that provide those resources. A proxy server thus functions on behalf of the client when requesting service, potentially masking the true origin of the request to the resource server.

PublicKey.label: Public Key
PublicKey.documentation: A public key can be disseminated widely as part of an asymmetric cryptography framework and be used to encrypt messages to send to the public key's owner or to authenticate signed messages from that sender.

PythonPackage.label: Python Package
PythonPackage.documentation: A Python package is an aggregation of many Python files - either in source code or in bytecode - and associated metadata and resources (text, images, etc.). Python packages can be distributed in different file formats.

Q-Learning.label: Q-Learning
Q-Learning.documentation: Q-learning is a model-free reinforcement learning algorithm to learn the value of an action in a particular state. It does not require a model of the environment (hence "model-free"), and it can handle problems with stochastic transitions and rewards without requiring adaptations.

QueryByCommittee.label: Query By Committee
QueryByCommittee.documentation: Query by Committee (QBC) takes inspiration from ensemble methods. Instead of just one classifier, it takes into account the decision of a committee C=ℎ1,…,ℎc of classifiers ℎi. Each classifier has the same target classes, but a different underlying model or a different view on the data.

RAM.label: RAM
RAM.documentation: Random-access memory (RAM) is a form of computer memory that can be read and changed in any order, typically used to store working data and machine code.

RD-0001.label: Acquire Infrastructure - SPARTA
RD-0001.documentation: Adversaries assemble the people, platforms, and plumbing they will later use to observe, reach, or impersonate mission components. Infrastructure spans RF and optical ground assets (antennas, modems, timing sources, front-ends), compute and storage (on-prem and cloud), network presence (leased ASNs/IP space, VPS fleets, CDN relays), identity fabric (burner accounts, domains, certificates), and fabrication/test environments for hardware and software. They favor assets that are inexpensive, deniable, and geographically diverse, mixing self-hosted gear with commercial services and compromised third-party systems. To support spacecraft operations, they may build SDR-based labs that replicate waveforms and framing, stage command/telemetry tooling behind traffic mixers, and pre-position data pipelines for collection and analysis. The objective is persistence and flexibility: the ability to pivot between reconnaissance, delivery, and command with minimal attribution risk.

RD-0001.01.label: Ground Station Equipment - SPARTA
RD-0001.01.documentation: Rather than compromising existing stations, adversaries may acquire or assemble their own RF ground stack.
