WebApplicationServer.documentation: A web application server is a web server that hosts applications. Application server frameworks are software frameworks for building application servers. An application server framework provides both facilities to create web applications and a server environment to run them. In the case of Java application servers, the server behaves like an extended virtual machine for running applications, transparently handling connections to the database on one side, and, often, connections to the Web client on the other.

WebAuthentication.label: Web Authentication
WebAuthentication.documentation: A request-response comprising a user credential presentation to a system and a verification response where the verifying party is a web server.

WebFileResource.label: Web File Resource
WebFileResource.documentation: A web file resource is a file resource identified by a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) and made available from one host to another host via a web protocol and across a network or networks.

WebIdentityToken.label: Web Identity Token
WebIdentityToken.documentation: An ID token is an artifact that proves that the user has been authenticated.

WebNetworkTraffic.label: Web Network Traffic
WebNetworkTraffic.documentation: Web network traffic is network traffic that uses a standard web protocol.

WebResource.label: Web Resource
WebResource.documentation: A web resource is a resource identified by a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) and made available from one host to another host via a web protocol and across a network or networks.

WebResourceAccess.label: Web Resource Access
WebResourceAccess.documentation: Ephemeral digital artifact comprising a request of a network resource and any response from that network resource using a standard web protocol.

WebScriptFile.label: Web Script File
WebScriptFile.documentation: A file containing a script in a web-scripting programming language. Web scripts may be present and run on the client or on the server side.

WebServer.label: Web Server
WebServer.documentation: A web server is server software, or hardware dedicated to running this software, that can satisfy client requests on the World Wide Web. A web server can, in general, contain one or more websites. A web server processes incoming network requests over HTTP and several other related protocols. While the major function is to serve content, a full implementation of HTTP also includes ways of receiving content from clients. This feature is used for submitting web forms, including uploading of files.

WebServerApplication.label: Web Server Application
WebServerApplication.documentation: A web server application handles HTTP requests from clients, serves static content, and may act as a reverse proxy or load balancer.

WebSessionAccessMediation.label: Web Session Access Mediation
WebSessionAccessMediation.documentation: Web session access mediation secures user sessions in web applications by employing robust authentication and integrity validation, along with adaptive threat mitigation techniques, to ensure that access to web resources is authorized and protected from session-related attacks.

WebSessionActivityAnalysis.label: Web Session Activity Analysis
WebSessionActivityAnalysis.documentation: Monitoring changes in user web session behavior by comparing current web session activity to a baseline behavior profile or a catalog of predetermined malicious behavior.

WeightedMean.label: Weighted Mean
WeightedMean.documentation: A mean that incorporates weighting to certain data elements.

WideAreaNetwork.label: Wide Area Network
WideAreaNetwork.documentation: By contrast to a local area network (LAN), a wide area network (WAN), not only covers a larger geographic distance, but also generally involves leased telecommunication circuits or Internet links.

WindowOpenFile.label: Windows OpenFile
WindowOpenFile.documentation: Creates, opens, reopens, or deletes a file.

WindowsCreateFileA.label: Windows CreateFileA
WindowsCreateFileA.documentation: Creates or opens a file or I/O device. The most commonly used I/O devices are as follows: file, file stream, directory, physical disk, volume, console buffer, tape drive, communications resource, mailslot, and pipe. The function returns a handle that can be used to access the file or device for various types of I/O depending on the file or device and the flags and attributes specified.

WindowsCreateProcessA.label: Windows CreateProcessA
WindowsCreateProcessA.documentation: Creates a new process and its primary thread. The new process runs in the security context of the calling process.

WindowsCreateRemoteThread.label: Windows CreateRemoteThread
WindowsCreateRemoteThread.documentation: Creates a thread that runs in the virtual address space of another process.

WindowsCreateThread.label: Windows CreateThread
WindowsCreateThread.documentation: Creates a thread to execute within the virtual address space of the calling process.

WindowsDuplicateToken.label: Windows DuplicateToken
WindowsDuplicateToken.documentation: The DuplicateToken function creates a new access token that duplicates one already in existence.

WindowsGetThreadContext.label: Windows GetThreadContext
WindowsGetThreadContext.documentation: Retrieves the context of the specified thread.

WindowsNtAllocateVirtualMemory.label: Windows NtAllocateVirtualMemory
WindowsNtAllocateVirtualMemory.documentation: The NtAllocateVirtualMemory routine reserves, commits, or both, a region of pages within the user-mode virtual address space of a specified process.

WindowsNtCreateFile.label: Windows NtCreateFile
WindowsNtCreateFile.documentation: Creates a new file or directory, or opens an existing file, device, directory, or volume.

WindowsNtCreateMailslotFile.label: Windows NtCreateMailslotFile
WindowsNtCreateMailslotFile.documentation: Creates a special File Object called Mailslot.

WindowsNtCreatePagingFile.label: Windows NtCreatePagingFile
WindowsNtCreatePagingFile.documentation: Typically used by Control Panel's "System" applet for creating new paged files.

WindowsNtDuplicateToken.label: Windows NtDuplicateToken
WindowsNtDuplicateToken.documentation: The NtDuplicateToken function creates a handle to a new access token that duplicates an existing token. This function can create either a primary token or an impersonation token.

WindowsNtFreeVirtualMemory.label: Windows NtFreeVirtualMemory
WindowsNtFreeVirtualMemory.documentation: The NtFreeVirtualMemory routine releases, decommits, or both releases and decommits, a region of pages within the virtual address space of a specified process.

WindowsNtOpenFile.label: Windows NtOpenFile
WindowsNtOpenFile.documentation: The NtOpenFile routine opens an existing file, directory, device, or volume.

WindowsNtOpenProcess.label: Windows NtOpenProcess
WindowsNtOpenProcess.documentation: Opens a handle to process object and sets the access rights to this object.

WindowsNtOpenThread.label: Windows NtOpenThread
WindowsNtOpenThread.documentation: Opens a handle to a thread object with the access specified.

WindowsNtQuerySystemTime.label: Windows NtQuerySystemTime
WindowsNtQuerySystemTime.documentation: Returns current time in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) 8-bytes format.

WindowsNtReadFile.label: Windows NtReadFile
WindowsNtReadFile.documentation: The NtReadFile routine reads data from an open file.

WindowsNtReadFileScatter.label: Windows NtReadFileScatter
WindowsNtReadFileScatter.documentation: Reads specified block from file into multiple buffers. Each buffer must have one page length.

WindowsNtSetInformationFileArgumentFileD.label: Windows NtSetInformationFile Argument FileDispositionInformation
WindowsNtSetInformationFileArgumentFileD.documentation: Request to delete the file when it is closed or cancel a previously requested deletion.

WindowsNtWriteFile.label: Windows NtWriteFile
WindowsNtWriteFile.documentation: Writes data to an open file.

WindowsNtWriteFileGather.label: Windows NtWriteFileGather
WindowsNtWriteFileGather.documentation: Writes specified block of file with data from memory pages.

WindowsOpenProcess.label: Windows OpenProcess
WindowsOpenProcess.documentation: Opens an existing local process object.

WindowsQueryPerformanceCounter.label: Windows QueryPerformanceCounter
WindowsQueryPerformanceCounter.documentation: Retrieves the current value of the performance counter, which is a high resolution (<1us) time stamp that can be used for time-interval measurements.

WindowsReadFile.label: Windows ReadFile
WindowsReadFile.documentation: Reads data from the specified file or input/output (I/O) device. Reads occur at the position specified by the file pointer if supported by the device.

WindowsRegistry.label: Windows Registry
WindowsRegistry.documentation: The Windows Registry is a hierarchical database that stores low-level settings for the Microsoft Windows operating system and for applications that opt to use the registry. The kernel, device drivers, services, Security Accounts Manager, and user interface can all use the registry. The registry also allows access to counters for profiling system performance.

WindowsRegistryEvent.label: Windows Registry Event
WindowsRegistryEvent.documentation: Events involving interactions with the Windows Registry, including keys, values, and associated security configurations.

WindowsRegistryKey.label: Windows Registry Key
WindowsRegistryKey.documentation: Windows Registry Keys are container objects similar to folders that contain subkeys and/or data entries called values. A key can be a 'Registry Hive' when it is root key of a logical group of keys, subkeys, and values that has a set of supporting files loaded into memory when the operating system is started or a user logs in.

WindowsRegistryKeyCreationEvent.label: Windows Registry Key Creation Event
WindowsRegistryKeyCreationEvent.documentation: An event where a new registry key is added to the Windows Registry, establishing a new hierarchical node for configuration.

WindowsRegistryKeyDeletionEvent.label: Windows Registry Key Deletion Event
WindowsRegistryKeyDeletionEvent.documentation: An event representing the removal of a registry key from the Windows Registry, including its hierarchical structure and associated metadata.

WindowsRegistryKeyEvent.label: Windows Registry Key Event
WindowsRegistryKeyEvent.documentation: Events representing actions performed on Windows Registry keys, such as creation, modification, or deletion, which define hierarchical nodes for storing configuration data.

WindowsRegistryKeyExportEvent.label: Windows Registry Key Export Event
WindowsRegistryKeyExportEvent.documentation: An event representing the export of registry key data from the Windows Registry to an external file or format.

WindowsRegistryKeyImportEvent.label: Windows Registry Key Import Event
WindowsRegistryKeyImportEvent.documentation: An event where registry key data is imported into the Windows Registry from an external source.

WindowsRegistryKeyReadEvent.label: Windows Registry Key Read Event
WindowsRegistryKeyReadEvent.documentation: An event where a registry key is accessed to query its structure, properties, or associated metadata without modifying its state.

WindowsRegistryKeyRenamingEvent.label: Windows Registry Key Renaming Event
WindowsRegistryKeyRenamingEvent.documentation: An event where the name of a registry key is changed, altering its identifier within the registry hierarchy.

WindowsRegistryKeyRestoreEvent.label: Windows Registry Key Restore Event
WindowsRegistryKeyRestoreEvent.documentation: An event where a registry key is restored to a previous state using a backup or recovery mechanism.

WindowsRegistryKeySetSecurityEvent.label: Windows Registry Key Set Security Event
WindowsRegistryKeySetSecurityEvent.documentation: An event representing the application or modification of access controls or security settings to a registry key.

WindowsRegistryKeyUpdateEvent.label: Windows Registry Key Update Event
WindowsRegistryKeyUpdateEvent.documentation: An event where an existing registry key is updated or reconfigured, reflecting changes to its metadata or properties.

WindowsRegistryValue.label: Windows Registry Value
WindowsRegistryValue.documentation: A Windows Registry Value is a data structure consisting of a name, type, data (as a pointer), and the length. Windows Registry Values are always associated with a Windows Registry Key. They store the actual configuration data for the operating system and the programs that run on the system.

WindowsRegistryValueDeletionEvent.label: Windows Registry Value Deletion Event
WindowsRegistryValueDeletionEvent.documentation: An event where a registry value is deleted from the Windows Registry, permanently removing its associated data.

WindowsRegistryValueEvent.label: Windows Registry Value Event
WindowsRegistryValueEvent.documentation: Events representing actions performed on Windows Registry values, which store configuration data within registry keys.

WindowsRegistryValueGetEvent.label: Windows Registry Value Get Event
WindowsRegistryValueGetEvent.documentation: An event where the data of a registry value is retrieved, typically to read its configuration or state.

WindowsRegistryValueSetEvent.label: Windows Registry Value Set Event
WindowsRegistryValueSetEvent.documentation: An event where data is assigned to a registry value, either creating it or updating its existing content.

WindowsRegistryValueUpdateEvent.label: Windows Registry Value Update Event
WindowsRegistryValueUpdateEvent.documentation: An event indicating changes to the data or configuration of an existing registry value within the Windows Registry.

WindowsResumeThread.label: Windows ResumeThread
WindowsResumeThread.documentation: Decrements a thread's suspend count. When the suspend count is decremented to zero, the execution of the thread is resumed.

WindowsSetThreadContext.label: Windows SetThreadContext
WindowsSetThreadContext.documentation: Sets the context for the specified thread.

WindowsTerminateProcess.label: Windows TerminateProcess
WindowsTerminateProcess.documentation: Terminates the specified process and all of its threads.

WindowsVirtualAllocEx.label: Windows VirtualAllocEx
WindowsVirtualAllocEx.documentation: Reserves, commits, or changes the state of a region of memory within the virtual address space of a specified process. The function initializes the memory it allocates to zero.

WindowsVirtualFree.label: Windows VirtualFree
WindowsVirtualFree.documentation: Releases, decommits, or releases and decommits a region of pages within the virtual address space of the calling process.

WindowsVirtualProtectEx.label: Windows VirtualProtectEx
WindowsVirtualProtectEx.documentation: Changes the protection on a region of committed pages in the virtual address space of a specified process.

WindowsWriteFile.label: Windows WriteFile
WindowsWriteFile.documentation: Writes data to the specified file or input/output (I/O) device.

WindowsWriteProcessMemory.label: Windows WriteProcessMemory
WindowsWriteProcessMemory.documentation: Writes data to an area of memory in a specified process. The entire area to be written to must be accessible or the operation fails.

WiredLink.label: Wired Link
WiredLink.documentation: A physical link that uses a physical conductor or waveguide to constrain and direct signal propagation between endpoints. The signal is confined within or along a manufactured medium such as metal conductors, optical fibers, or coaxial structures.

WirelessAccessPoint.label: Wireless Access Point
WirelessAccessPoint.documentation: In computer networking, a wireless access point (WAP), or more generally just access point (AP), is a networking hardware device that allows other Wi-Fi devices to connect to a wired network. The AP usually connects to a router (via a wired network) as a standalone device, but it can also be an integral component of the router itself. An AP is differentiated from a hotspot which is a physical location where Wi-Fi access is available.

WirelessAttacker.label: Wireless Attacker
WirelessAttacker.documentation: An attacker who targets wireless communication methods, like Wi-Fi, without needing physical access to the premises.

WirelessLink.label: Wireless Link
WirelessLink.documentation: A physical link that transmits signals through free space or an unguided medium without physical connectors between endpoints. The signal propagates through air, vacuum, water, or other natural media using electromagnetic waves or acoustic energy.

WirelessRouter.label: Wireless Router
WirelessRouter.documentation: A wireless router is a device that performs the functions of a router and also includes the functions of a wireless access point. It is used to provide access to the Internet or a private computer network. Depending on the manufacturer and model, it can function in a wired local area network, in a wireless-only LAN, or in a mixed wired and wireless network.

WriteFile.label: Write File
WriteFile.documentation: The write is one of the most basic routines provided by a Unix-like operating system kernel. It writes data from a buffer declared by the user to a given device, such as a file. This is the primary way to output data from a program by directly using a system call. The destination is identified by a numeric code. The data to be written, for instance a piece of text, is defined by a pointer and a size, given in number of bytes. write thus takes three arguments.

WriteProtectSwitch.label: Write Protect Switch
WriteProtectSwitch.documentation: A physical device used to restrict configuration of a device.

ZeroClientComputer.label: Zero Client Computer
ZeroClientComputer.documentation: Zero client is also referred as ultra thin client, contains no moving parts but centralizes all processing and storage to just what is running on the server. As a result, it requires no local driver to install, no patch management, and no local operating system licensing fees or updates. The device consumes very little power and is tamper-resistant and completely incapable of storing any data locally, providing a more secure endpoint.

abuses.label: abuses
abuses.documentation: x abuses y: The entity x applies an artifact y to a wrong thing or person; x applies y badly or incorrectly.

access-mediated-by.label: access-mediated-by
access-mediated-by.documentation: x access-mediated-by y: The entity or resource x has its access regulated, controlled, or facilitated by entity y, which acts as an intermediary or gatekeeper to enforce access control policies.

accessed-by.label: accessed-by
accessed-by.documentation: x accessed-by y: The entity or resource x is accessed by entity y.

accesses.label: accesses
accesses.documentation: x accesses y: The subject x takes the action of reading from, writing into, or executing the stored information in the object y. Reads, writes, and executes are specific cases of accesses.

addressed-by.label: addressed-by
addressed-by.documentation: x addressed-by y: Relates a resource x (e.g., network host, peripheral device, disk sector, a memory cell or other logical or physical entity) to a discrete address y in an address space that points to it.

addresses.label: addresses
addresses.documentation: x addresses y: Relates a pointer x to a digital artifact y located in the address space to which x points. The address space is part of some digital store, whether it be in memory, an image, or a persistent storage device.

adds.label: adds
adds.documentation: x adds y: The subject x adds a data object y, such as a file, to some other digital artifact, such as a directory. Examples include an agent or technique adding a record to a database or a domain entry to a DNS server.

analyzes.label: analyzes
analyzes.documentation: x analyzes y: The subject x breaks down object y into components or essential features, assessing y by quantitative methods, qualitative methods, or both.  Usually the analysis is done in terms of some model or framework.

associated-with.label: associated-with
associated-with.documentation: x associated-with y: The subject x and object y are associated in some way.  This is the most general definite relationship in d3fend (i.e., most general relationship that is not prefixed by 'may-'.)

attached-to.label: attached-to
attached-to.documentation: x attached-to y: A subject x is joined in close association to an object y.

attack-id.label: attack-id
attack-id.documentation: x attack-id y: The offensive technique x has the att&ck unique id of y.

attack-kb-annotation.label: attack-kb-annotation
attack-kb-annotation.documentation: x attack-kb-annotation y: The offensive technique x has the kb annotation of y.

authenticates.label: authenticates
authenticates.documentation: x authenticates y: The subject x establishes the authenticity of some y. This relation indicates an authentication event has occurred.

authorizes.label: authorizes
authorizes.documentation: x authorizes y: A subject x grants authorization or clearance for an agent y to use an object.  This relation indicates an authorization event has occurred.

available.label: date available
available.documentation: Date that the resource became or will become available.

blocks.label: blocks
blocks.documentation: x blocks y: The entity x blocks off the use of digital artifact y by reference to a block or allow list (or both.)

broader.label: broader
broader.documentation: x broader y: The entity x represents a more general or inclusive concept than entity y.

broader-transitive.label: broader-transitive
broader-transitive.documentation: x broader-transitive y: The entity x represents a more general concept than entity y, including indirect or hierarchical relationships where x encompasses y through intermediate entities.

capec-id.label: capec-id
capec-id.documentation: Unique identifier for a CAPEC technique, i.e. a common attack pattern identified by the pattern CAPEC-[number].

carried-by.label: carried-by
carried-by.documentation: x carried-by y: The information entity x is dependent upon the entity y for its storage, transport, or communication. Entity y serves as the necessary bearer or link from which x can be recovered or interpreted.

carries.label: carries
carries.documentation: x carries y: The entity x serves as the bearer or link for information y, enabling y to be stored, transported, or communicated such that y can be recovered or interpreted from x

caused-by.label: caused-by
caused-by.documentation: x caused-by y: The event or action x occurs as a consequence of event or action y.

causes.label: causes
causes.documentation: x causes y: The event or action x brings about event or action y as a consequence.

comments.label: comments
comments.documentation: x comments y: x claim has provider comments y.

communicates-with.label: communicates-with
communicates-with.documentation: x communicates-with y: x and y exchange signals or data bidirectionally, enabling mutual awareness, coordination, or interaction.

configures.label: configures
configures.documentation: x configures y: The entity x sets the operational parameters of entity y, determining how y will operate.

connected-to.label: connected-to
connected-to.documentation: x connected-to y: The subject x shares a direct physical or logical link with object y such that communication is possible between them without intermediate routing.

connects.label: connects
connects.documentation: x connects y: The subject x joins system y by means of communication equipment (to some other system, typically the adversary-targeted host).

contained-by.label: contained-by
contained-by.documentation: x contained-by y: The entity x exists within or is physically or logically enclosed by entity y.

contains.label: contains
contains.documentation: x contains y: A core relation that holds between a whole x and its part y.  Equivalent to relational concept 'has part' and thus transitive.

controlled-by.label: controlled-by
controlled-by.documentation: x controlled-by y: x's operation or behavior is directed or regulated by y.

controls.label: controls
controls.documentation: x controls y: x directs or regulates y's operational state, behavior, or function.

copies.label: copies
copies.documentation: x copies y: A technique or agent x reproduces or makes an exact copy of some digital artifact y.

copy-of.label: copy-of
copy-of.documentation: x copy-of y: The subject x is a duplicate of the object y.

corrupts.label: corrupts
corrupts.documentation: x corrupts y: The entity x causes y to enter an incorrect, inconsistent, or unintended state by modifying y's information-bearing content (e.g., a bit, symbol, word, configuration cell, or stored parameter) such that y's value no longer matches the expected or previously valid value.

created.label: date created
created.documentation: Date of creation of the resource.

created-by.label: created-by
created-by.documentation: x created-by y: The entity x is brought into existence, developed, or generated by entity y.

creates.label: creates
creates.documentation: x creates y: The subject x brings into existence an object y. Some technique or agent x creates a persistent digital artifact y (as opposed to production of a consumable or transient object.); i.e., bring forth or generate.

d3fend-annotation.label: d3fend-annotation
d3fend-annotation.documentation: x d3fend-annotation y: The d3fend object x has the annotation y.

d3fend-artifact-data-property.label: d3fend-artifact-data-property
d3fend-artifact-data-property.documentation: x d3fend-artifact-data-property y: The artifact x has the data property y.

d3fend-comment.label: d3fend-comment
d3fend-comment.documentation: x d3fend-comment y: The entity x has an D3FEND team written a public note about entity y.

d3fend-display-property.label: d3fend-display-property
d3fend-display-property.documentation: x d3fend-display-property y: An object x should be displayed using the display property y, when it applies.

d3fend-id.label: d3fend-id
d3fend-id.documentation: Unique identifier for a D3FEND technique. D3-[Acronym].

d3fend-kb-annotation-property.label: d3fend-kb-annotation-property
d3fend-kb-annotation-property.documentation: x d3fend-kb-annotation-property y: The entity x had the d3fend kb annotation y.

d3fend-kb-data-property.label: d3fend-kb-data-property
d3fend-kb-data-property.documentation: x d3fend-kb-data-property y: The d3fend knowledge base object x has a data property y; e.g., a string capturing a particular aspect or section of a knowledge base article.

d3fend-kb-object-property.label: d3fend-kb-object-property
d3fend-kb-object-property.documentation: x d3fend-kb-object-property y: The object y is a d3fend knowledge base object property. These properties allow the linkage of knowledge and information supporting and illustrating the d3fend model.

d3fend-kb-reference-annotation.label: d3fend-kb-reference-annotation
d3fend-kb-reference-annotation.documentation: x d3fend-kb-data-property y: The reference x has the data property y.

date.label: date
date.documentation: A point or period of time associated with an event in the lifecycle of the resource.

deceives-with.label: deceives-with
deceives-with.documentation: x deceives-with y: The entity x misleads or manipulates another entity using y as a tool, method, or mechanism to create false perceptions or understanding.

decodes.label: decodes
decodes.documentation: x decodes y: The entity x transforms data y to a different form, usually through decompression.

definition.label: definition
definition.documentation: x definition y: The d3fend object x has the definition y.

deletes.label: deletes
deletes.documentation: x deletes y: A technique or agent x wipes out the digitally or magnetically recorded information of digital object y.

dependent.label: dependent
dependent.documentation: x dependent y: A dependent y is an entity that requires the fulfillment of the requirements specified in dependency x.

depends-on.label: depends-on
depends-on.documentation: x depends-on y: The entity x is contingent on y being available; x relies on y.

derived-from.label: derived-from
derived-from.documentation: x derived-from y: The entity x is derived from or based on the value of y.

description.label: description
description.documentation: A statement that represents something in words.

detects.label: detects
detects.documentation: x detects y: The entity x discovers the presence, occurrence, or state of entity y through observation or measurement.

disables.label: disables
disables.documentation: x disables y: The technique or agent x makes an entity y unable to perform its actions or capabilities.

display-baseurl.label: display-baseurl
display-baseurl.documentation: A base string to use as prefix to create a full URL for an entity. The baseurl must end in a forward slash: /

display-order.label: display-order
display-order.documentation: x display-order y: An object x should be displayed in ordinal position y when placed or listed in a d3fend display with other objects of its kind.

drives.label: drives
drives.documentation: x drives y: The device driver x causes a system component y to function by controlling it.

employed-by.label: employed-by
employed-by.documentation: x employed-by y: An entity x is put into service by a technique or agent y. Inverse of y employs x.

employs.label: employs
employs.documentation: x employs y: The entity x makes purposeful use of entity y to perform a function.

enabled-by.label: enabled-by
enabled-by.documentation: x enabled-by y: A top level technique y enables a tactic x, that is, the property indicates that a technique y is used to put a particular tactic x into action. In other words, y renders x capable or able for some task.  Inverse of enables.

enables.label: enables
enables.documentation: x enables y: A top level technique x enables a tactic y, that is, the property indicates that a technique x is used to put a particular tactic y into action. In other words, x renders y capable or able for some task.

encodes.label: encodes
encodes.documentation: x encodes y: The entity x transforms data y to a different form, usually through compression.

encrypts.label: encrypts
encrypts.documentation: x encrypts y: The entity x converts the ordinary representation of a digital artifact y into a secret code.

enforces.label: enforces
enforces.documentation: x enforces y: Technique x forces entity y to be compliant with a law, rule, or obligation.

enumerates.label: enumerates
enumerates.documentation: x enumerates y: The subject x takes the action of reading from a digital source y to acquire data and create a list of its contents.

erases.label: erases
erases.documentation: x erases y: A technique x removes recorded data from storage device y creating space for new data.

evaluated-by.label: evaluated-by
evaluated-by.documentation: x evaluated-by y: The entity x is assessed and analyzed by entity y.

evaluates.label: evaluates
evaluates.documentation: x evaluates y: The entity x systematically assesses entity y to judge its state, quality, or risk.

evicts.label: evicts
evicts.documentation: x evicts y: The entity x forcibly removes entity y from the environment or resource where y was residing.

exactly.label: exactly
exactly.documentation: x exactly y: The entity x is identical to or fully corresponds to entity y.

excises.label: excises
excises.documentation: x excises y: Technique x removes a section of entity y.

executed-by.label: executed-by
executed-by.documentation: x executed-by y: The entity or function x is carried out, performed, or run by entity y.

executes.label: executes
executes.documentation: x executes y: The subject x takes the action of carrying out (executing) y, which is a single software module, function, or instruction.

extends.label: extends
extends.documentation: x extends y: The entity x extends the scope or range or area of entity y, especially in the sense of widening the range of applications.

filters.label: filters
filters.documentation: x filters y: An technique or agent x removes some specified set of of entities from the content of a digital artifact y, by passing an artifact's content through a filter.  A filter is a device that removes something from whatever passes through it.

forges.label: forges
forges.documentation: x forges y: An technique or agent x counterfeits a digital artifact y, such as a fake credential, with the intent to deceive.

hardens.label: hardens
hardens.documentation: x hardens y: The entity x fortifies entity y to reduce its weaknesses so y can better withstand attack or failure.

has-account.label: has-account
has-account.documentation: x has-account y: The subject x has ownership or possession of some account y.

has-agent.label: has-agent
has-agent.documentation: x has-agent y: The event x occurs because agent y actively carries it out.

has-dependent.label: has-dependent
has-dependent.documentation: x has-dependent y: The entity x is relied upon or required by entity y.

has-input.label: has-input
has-input.documentation: x has-input y: An event x has input y iff y is an artifact that is present at the start of x, provides material or information required for x to begin, and during x either y's state is altered or the information content it bears is realized.

has-link.label: has-link
has-link.documentation: x has-link y: The d3fend analysis x has the link y.

has-location.label: has-location
has-location.documentation: x has-location y: The entity x is situated in a particular spot or position y.

has-mediator.label: has-mediator
has-mediator.documentation: x has-mediator y: The entity x relies on or is facilitated by entity y.

has-operating-mode.label: has-operating-mode
has-operating-mode.documentation: x has-operating-mode y: The entity x is currently operating in or has the potential to be in operating mode y.

has-output.label: has-output
has-output.documentation: x has-output y: An event x has output y iff y is an artifact that is present at the end of x, was not present in the same state at the start of x, and whose presence at the end is required for x to be considered complete; the change in state may arise either from a transformation of y itself or from the realization of the information content y bears.

has-participant.label: has-participant
has-participant.documentation: x has-participant y: The event x involves an object y as a participant, indicating that y plays some role in the event, whether actively, passively, or otherwise.

has-recipient.label: has-recipient
has-recipient.documentation: x has-recipient y: An agent y is the intended recipient and decoder of the information contained in communication x.

has-sender.label: has-sender
has-sender.documentation: x has-sender y: An agent y is the sender and encoder of the information contained in communication x.

has-weakness.label: has-weakness
has-weakness.documentation: x has-weakness y: The entity x exhibits a condition y that could, in some circumstances, lead to a vulnerability.

hides.label: hides
hides.documentation: x hides y: A technique or operation x conceals the digital artifact y.

identified-by.label: identified-by
identified-by.documentation: x identified-by y: The entity x is recognized or described by entity y.

identifies.label: identifies
identifies.documentation: x identifies y: The entity x recognizes or brings attention to entity y, making it distinct or clear through naming, description, or discovery.

impairs.label: impairs
impairs.documentation: x impairs y: The entity or action x hinders entity y by reducing its normal function, capacity, or availability.

implemented-by.label: implemented-by
implemented-by.documentation: x implemented-by y: The entity x is realized or brought into operation by entity y.

implements.label: implements
implements.documentation: x implements y: The entity x realizes entity y by putting its design or specification into effect.

initiates.label: initiates
initiates.documentation: x initiates y: The entity or action x starts or triggers entity or function y, bringing it into action.

injects.label: injects
injects.documentation: x injects y: The subject x takes the action of exploiting a security flaw by introducing (injecting) y, which is code or data that will change the course of execution or state of a computing process to an alternate course or state. Typically code injection is associated with adversaries intending the alternate course to facilitate a malevolent purpose; however, code injection can be unintentional or the intentions behind it may be good or benign.

input-of.label: input-of
input-of.documentation: x input-of y: An artifact x is input of an event y iff x participates at the start of y, provides the material or information required for y to begin, and during y either x's state is altered or the information content it bears is realized.

installs.label: installs
installs.documentation: x installs y: An entity x sets up digital artifact y for subsequent use.  For example, an installation program can install application software.

instructed-by.label: instructed-by
instructed-by.documentation: x instructed-by y: A subject x takes machine instructions from object y.

instructs.label: instructs
instructs.documentation: x instructs y: A subject x delivers machine instructions to object y.

interprets.label: interprets
interprets.documentation: x interprets y: The subject x interprets the executable script y. The definition of interprets here is 'Parse the source code and perform its behavior directly.'

inventoried-by.label: inventoried-by
inventoried-by.documentation: x inventoried-by y: The entity x is cataloged, recorded, or tracked by entity y.

inventories.label: inventories
inventories.documentation: x inventories y: The entity x systematically discovers entity y and records its presence and key details for tracking.

invoked-by.label: invoked-by
invoked-by.documentation: x invoked-by y: The entity x is called, triggered, or activated by entity y.

invokes.label: invokes
invokes.documentation: x invokes y: The subject x invokes a system service by use of an instruction object y that interrupts the program being executed and passes control to the operating system to perform that operation.

isolates.label: isolates
isolates.documentation: x isolates y: The technique or agent x sets digital artifact y apart from other digital artifacts, sequestering y.

issued.label: date issued
issued.documentation: Date of formal issuance of the resource.

jams.label: jams
jams.documentation: x jams y: The entity x deliberately introduces interfering energy that degrades, disrupts, blocks, or masks the information-bearing capability of the target y.

kb-abstract.label: kb-abstract
kb-abstract.documentation: x kb-abstract y: The reference x has the abstract y.

kb-article.label: kb-article
kb-article.documentation: The technique x has the kb-article y, where y is written in Markdown.

kb-author.label: kb-author
kb-author.documentation: x kb-author y: The reference x has some author y.

kb-mitre-analysis.label: kb-mitre-analysis
kb-mitre-analysis.documentation: x kb-mitre-analysis y: The reference x has the mitre d3fend analysis y.

kb-organization.label: kb-organization
kb-organization.documentation: x kb-organization y: The reference x was created or owned by the organization y.

kb-reference-of.label: kb-reference-of
kb-reference-of.documentation: x kb-is-example-of y: The reference x is an example of technique y.

kb-reference-title.label: kb-reference-title
kb-reference-title.documentation: x kb-reference-title y: The d3fend knowledge base reference x has the reference title string y.

limits.label: limits
limits.documentation: x limits y: The entity x specifies a designated limit beyond which some entity y cannot function or must be terminated.

loaded-by.label: loaded-by
loaded-by.documentation: x loaded-by y: The entity x is brought into memory by entity y.

loads.label: loads
loads.documentation: x loads y: The technique or process x transfers a software from storage y to a computer's memory for subsequent execution.

manages.label: manages
manages.documentation: x manages y: The technique or agent x watches and directs the use of digital artifact y.

mapped-by.label: mapped-by
mapped-by.documentation: x mapped-by y: The entity x is linked to another entity by entity y.

maps.label: maps
maps.documentation: x maps y: The entity x discovers and records how entity y is arranged and interconnected.

may-access.label: may-access
may-access.documentation: x may-access y: The entity x may access the thing y; that is, 'x accesses y' may be true.

may-add.label: may-add
may-add.documentation: x may-add y: The entity x may add the thing y; that is, 'x adds y' may be true.

may-be-associated-with.label: may-be-associated-with
may-be-associated-with.documentation: x may-be-associated-with y: The subject x and object y may be associated in some way.

may-be-tactically-associated-with.label: may-be-tactically-associated-with
may-be-tactically-associated-with.documentation: x may-be-tactically-associated-with y: the defensive action x may be a tactic that counters offensive action y.

may-block.label: may-block
may-block.documentation: x may-block y: They entity x may block the thing y; that is, 'x blocks y' may be true.

may-contain.label: may-contain
may-contain.documentation: to potentially have as contents or constituent parts; comprise; include.

may-corrupt.label: may-corrupt
may-corrupt.documentation: x may-corrupt y: They entity x may corrupt y's information content; that is, 'x corrupts y' may be true.

may-create.label: may-create
may-create.documentation: x may-create y: The entity x may create the entity y; that is, 'x creates y' may be true.

may-execute.label: may-execute
may-execute.documentation: x may-execute y: The subject x may take the action of carrying out (executing) y, which is a single software module, function, or instruction.

may-interpret.label: may-interpret
may-interpret.documentation: x may-interpret y: The entity x may interpret the thing y; that is, 'x interprets y' may be true.

may-invoke.label: may-invoke
may-invoke.documentation: x may-invoke y: The entity x may invoke the thing y; that is, 'x invokes y' may be true.

may-modify.label: may-modify
may-modify.documentation: x may-modify y: The entity x may modify the thing y; that is, 'x modifies y' may be true.

may-produce.label: may-produce
may-produce.documentation: x may-produce y: The entity x may produce the thing y; that is, 'x produces y' may be true.

may-run.label: may-run
may-run.documentation: x may-run y: The entity x may run the thing y; that is, 'x runs y' may be true.

may-transfer.label: may-transfer
may-transfer.documentation: x may-transfer y: They entity x may send the thing y; that is, 'x transfers y' may be true.

mediates-access-to.label: mediates-access-to
mediates-access-to.documentation: x mediates-access-to y: The entity x controls and brokers requests to reach entity y, enforcing the access rules that allow or deny it.

modified.label: date modified
modified.documentation: Date on which the resource was changed.

modified-by.label: modified-by
modified-by.documentation: x modified-by y: The entity x is changed by entity y.

modifies.label: modifies
modifies.documentation: x modifies y: A technique or agent x causes a digital object y to change; become different; or undertake a transformation.  Afterwards, the data or state held by a digital object is changed.

modifies-part.label: modifies-part
modifies-part.documentation: x modifies-part y: The entity x modifies a part of y.  [Note: This is a rolification property for the rule 'if one modifies a part of a whole, they modify the whole.'  Reasoning for this and similar semantics to come are under evaluation and not part of current d3fend inferences.]

monitors.label: monitors
monitors.documentation: x monitors y: The technique or agent x keep tabs on, keeps an eye on, or keeps the digital artifact y under surveillance.

narrower.label: narrower
narrower.documentation: x narrower y: The entity x represents a more specific or focused concept than entity y.

narrower-transitive.label: narrower-transitive
narrower-transitive.documentation: x narrower-transitive y: The entity x represents a more specific concept than entity y, including indirect or hierarchical relationships where x is a subset of y through intermediate entities.

neutralizes.label: neutralizes
neutralizes.documentation: x neutralizes y: The technique x makes the execution of actions of y ineffective by preventing or counterbalancing the effect of y.

obfuscates.label: obfuscates
obfuscates.documentation: x obfuscates y: The technique x makes the digital artifact y unclear or obscure.  Typically obfuscation is a way to hide a digital artifact from discovery, use, or both.

operates.label: operates
operates.documentation: x operates y: The entity x enables, activates, or controls the functioning or behavior of object y (operated entity), typically in accordance with the design or intended use of the operated entity.

operating-system.label: operating-system
operating-system.documentation: x operating-system y: The product x is supported on operating system y.

originates-from.label: originates-from
originates-from.documentation: x originates-from y: The digital event or artifact x began its network transit from a physical location y.

output-of.label: output-of
output-of.documentation: x output-of y: An artifact x is output of an event y iff x must be present when y concludes, was absent in the same state when x began, and y counts as complete only when x is available at its end.

owns.label: owns
owns.documentation: x owns y: The subject x has ownership or possession of some object y.

participates-in.label: participates-in
participates-in.documentation: x participates-in y: The object x takes part in the event y, signifying that x contributes to or is affected by the event's occurrence in some way.

powered-by.label: powered-by
powered-by.documentation: x powered-by y: x obtains its essential energy or force from y to perform its function or remain active.

powers.label: powers
powers.documentation: x powers y: x furnishes y with the energy or force required for y's functionality or operation.

preceded-by.label: preceded-by
preceded-by.documentation: x preceded-by y: The event or action x occurs after event or action y in time.

precedes.label: precedes
precedes.documentation: x precedes y: The event or action x occurs before event or action y in time.

pref-label.label: pref-label
pref-label.documentation: x pref-label y: The preferred display value for x is y in d3fend tools.

process-ancestor.label: process-ancestor
process-ancestor.documentation: x process-ancestor y: The process y is a process ancestor of process x, indicating one or more process creation events were conducted at process y and subsequently created process x.

process-command-line-arguments.label: process-command-line-arguments
process-command-line-arguments.documentation: x process-command-line-arguments y: The process x has the process command line arguments data y.

process-data-property.label: process-data-property
process-data-property.documentation: x process-data-property y: The process x has the data property y.

process-environmental-variables.label: process-environmental-variables
process-environmental-variables.documentation: x process-environment-variables y: The process x has the process environmental variables data y.

process-identifier.label: process-identifier
process-identifier.documentation: x process-identifier y: The process x has the process identifier y.

process-image-path.label: process-image-path
process-image-path.documentation: x process-image-path y: The filepath y is the process image path for the process x, indicating the path to the resource from which the process's image was loaded.

process-parent.label: process-parent
process-parent.documentation: x process-parent y: The process y created the process x (directly) with a create process event.

process-property.label: process-property
process-property.documentation: x process-property y: The process x has the a process-property y.  This is generalization for specific process object properties.

process-security-context.label: process-security-context
process-security-context.documentation: x process-security-context y: The process x has the process security context data y.

process-user.label: process-user
process-user.documentation: x process-user y: The process x has been executed by the user y.

produced-by.label: produced-by
produced-by.documentation: x produced-by y: The entity x is created by entity y.

produces.label: produces
produces.documentation: x produces y: The subject entity x or process produces a data object y, which may be discrete digital object or a stream (e.g., a stream such as network traffic.)

provider.label: provider
provider.documentation: x provider y: A provider y is an entity that supplies a service, system, or data resources to a dependent entity x.

published.label: date published
published.documentation: Date of publication of the resource.

quarantines.label: quarantines
quarantines.documentation: x quarantines y: Technique x moves entity y to a place of isolation.

queries.label: queries
queries.documentation: x queries y: The entity x requests information or data from entity y.

reads.label: reads
reads.documentation: x reads y: The subject x takes the action of reading from a digital source y to acquire data and placing it into volatile memory for processing.

receives.label: receives
receives.documentation: x receives y: The subject x acquires object y from a communication medium and transfers y into its local context for storage or processing.

recorded-in.label: recorded-in
recorded-in.documentation: x recorded-in y: The event x is documented, logged, or otherwise preserved within the digital artifact y, which stores or encodes relevant data about the event.

records.label: records
records.documentation: x records y: The digital artifact x makes a record of events y; set down in permanent form.

regenerates.label: regenerates
regenerates.documentation: x regenerates y: The entity x discards the current digital artifact y and creates a new version that serves the same function.

related.label: related
related.documentation: x related y: x has a symmetric associative relation to y.

release-date.label: release-date
release-date.documentation: x release-date y: The object x has the release-date y.

restores.label: restores
restores.documentation: x restores y: The entity x returns entity y to its known-good or previous state.

restricted-by.label: restricted-by
restricted-by.documentation: x restricted-by y: The entity x is limited, constrained, or regulated by entity y.

restricts.label: restricts
restricts.documentation: x restricts y: The entity x bounds the use of entity y.

resume.label: resume
resume.documentation: x resume y: The agent or technique x continues a previous action on entity y. Usually occurs after suspension on y.

resumes.label: resumes
resumes.documentation: x resumes y: The agent or technique x continues a previous action on entity y. Usually occurs after suspension on y.

risk-impact.label: risk-impact
risk-impact.documentation: Risk impact rating, expressed on a numeric scale from 1 (lowest impact) to 5 (highest impact) in the context of a 5x5 risk matrix. Impact is used here as a synonym for consequence, another popular term used in risk analysis.

risk-likelihood.label: risk-likelihood
risk-likelihood.documentation: Risk likelihood rating, expressed on a numeric scale from 1 (lowest likelihood) to 5 (highest likelihood) in the context of a 5x5 risk matrix.

runs.label: runs
runs.documentation: x runs y: To carry out a process or program y, as on a computer or a machine x; where y may be a large software assembly or a specific module or instruction.  Examples: "run a new program on the Mac"; "the computer runs the application software".

semantic-relation.label: semantic-relation
semantic-relation.documentation: x semantic-relation y: The entity x is conceptually or meaningfully connected to entity y.

signed-by.label: signed-by
signed-by.documentation: x signed-by y: The digital artifact x includes a signature generated by the entity y, certifying the authenticity and integrity of x. This relationship indicates that x has undergone a validation process by y, using cryptographic measures to ensure that x is trustworthy and unaltered since the signing by y.

signs.label: signs
signs.documentation: x signs y: The entity x applies a digital signature to the digital artifact y, thereby asserting its validity, integrity, and authenticity. Typically, this involves cryptographic techniques to securely bind the signature to y, ensuring that y's contents have not been altered and are authentic as endorsed by x.

spoofs.label: spoofs
spoofs.documentation: x spoofs y: The technique x creates a fake instance of a digital artifact y; that is, y is a decoy, fake, or counterfeit.

strengthens.label: strengthens
strengthens.documentation: x strengthens y: The technique x makes digital artifact y resistant (to harm or misuse.)

summarizes.label: summarizes
summarizes.documentation: x summarizes y: The sensor x summarizes a set y of events concerning digital artifacts over time.

suspends.label: suspends
suspends.documentation: x suspends y: The agent or technique x pauses entity y.

t-SNEClustering.label: t-SNE Clustering
t-SNEClustering.documentation: T-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) is a statistical method for visualizing high-dimensional data by giving each datapoint a location in a two or three-dimensional map.

terminates.label: terminates
terminates.documentation: x terminates y: The technique x brings to an end or halt to some activity y.

text.label: text
text.documentation: The text of the document (i.e., terms of license.)

title.label: title
title.documentation: A name given to the resource.

transmits.label: transmits
transmits.documentation: x transmits y: The subject x actively emits object y onto a communication medium, rendering y observable and available for reception on that medium.

unloads.label: unloads
unloads.documentation: x unloads y: The technique or artifact performs the action of unloading some artifact (applications, kernel modules, or hardware drivers, etc.) from a computer's memory.

unmounts.label: unmounts
unmounts.documentation: x unmounts y: An operation x removes the access via computer system's file system the availability of files and directories on storage artifact y.  Unmounts reverse or undo prior mount operations.

updates.label: updates
updates.documentation: x updates y: The technique x updates the software for component y.

use-limits.label: use-limits
use-limits.documentation: x use-limits y: The entity x specifies a designated number of uses beyond which some entity y cannot function or must be terminated.

used-by.label: used-by
used-by.documentation: x used-by y: The inverse of y uses x.

uses.label: uses
uses.documentation: x uses y: The entity x puts into service a resource or implement y; makes y work or employ for a particular purpose or for its inherent or natural purpose.

valid.label: date valid
valid.documentation: Date (often a range) of validity of a resource.

validated-by.label: validated-by
validated-by.documentation: x validated-by y: The digital artifact x has its authenticity and correctness confirmed or verified by the technique, operation, or agent y.

validates.label: validates
validates.documentation: x validates y: The technique x proves the digital artifact y is valid; that is, x shows or confirms the validity of y.

verifies.label: verifies
verifies.documentation: x verifies y: The technique x confirms the truth of a digital artifact y.

version.label: version
version.documentation: x version y: The product or service x has the version y.

windows-registry-data-property.label: windows-registry-data-property
windows-registry-data-property.documentation: x windows-registry-data-property y: The windows registry entry x has the property y.

windows-registry-key.label: windows-registry-key
windows-registry-key.documentation: x value y: The key-value pair x has the key y.

windows-registry-value.label: windows-registry-value
windows-registry-value.documentation: x value y: The key-value pair x has the data value y.

writes.label: writes
writes.documentation: x writes y: The subject x takes the action of writing to a digital artifact y to store data and placing it into persistent memory for later reference.
